definition_zh: 天空的；天体的；天国的；文学用语中表示「超凡的、极美的」
definition_en: relating to the sky, to the bodies in it, or to heaven, especially in astronomy and religious writing
core_image: 夜里抬头，满天光点像钉在一张深蓝色穹顶上，地面之上的一切都挂在这张穹顶下面
scene: 天文台圆顶打开后，观测者把镜筒对准一片星群，记录它们缓慢移动的位置。The celestial map on the wall showed where each star would rise.
sceneCN: 这里 celestial 指「属于天空的、天上的」（第 1 个义项：与天空或天体有关）；句意为墙上的星空图显示了每颗星将从何处升起。图中可辨识物件：星空图、望远镜、圆顶、赤道仪。

pos.zh: 天空的；天体的；天国的
文学用法：超凡的；极美的

derivatives.zh: 天青石（以天空命名的锶矿物）
天青石的别名；亦用作颜色名

senses.title: Of the sky as a vault
senses.definition: belonging to the sky as seen from the earth, especially the vault in which the stars appear
senses.definitionCN: 属于从地面所见的天空，尤指星星所在的那层穹顶
senses.example: Ancient sailors read the celestial vault the way we read a map.
senses.exampleCN: 古代水手像我们读地图一样读那片天穹。
senses.why: caelum named the sky itself, so the adjective first describes anything that belongs to that vault.
senses.whyCN: caelum 本指天空本身，因此这个形容词最初描述一切属于那层穹顶的事物。

senses.title: Of a heavenly body
senses.definition: relating to a star, planet, moon or other object in space rather than to the earth
senses.definitionCN: 与恒星、行星、卫星等太空中的物体有关，而非与地球有关
senses.example: Celestial objects were charted long before their distances were known.
senses.exampleCN: 早在测出距离之前，天体就被绘制成图了。
senses.why: once the sky was filled with named bodies, the adjective naturally followed them.
senses.whyCN: 当天空被逐一命名出各种天体之后，这个形容词自然就跟着这些天体走了。

senses.title: Of heaven or the divine
senses.definition: belonging to heaven or to divine beings, especially in religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 属于天国或神灵，尤见于宗教文字
senses.example: The hymn describes a celestial choir that never rests.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗描绘了一支永不休止的天国合唱队。
senses.why: Latin caelum covered both the visible sky and the home of the gods, so the adjective kept both readings.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 caelum 既指可见的天空，也指众神的居所，因此这个形容词同时保留了这两层意思。

senses.title: Blissfully beautiful
senses.definition: so beautiful or blissful that it seems to belong to another world
senses.definitionCN: 美得像不属于这个世界，或幸福得如同身处另一世界
senses.example: The soprano's celestial tone silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 女高音那种超凡的音色让全场安静下来。
senses.why: the religious sense softened into a word for beauty that seems not to be of this earth.
senses.whyCN: 宗教义逐渐柔化，转指仿佛不属于人间的美。

senses.title: Of a star map or globe
senses.definition: relating to a map or globe that represents the sky as a surface
senses.definitionCN: 与把天空画成一个曲面的星图或天球仪有关
senses.example: A celestial globe shows the constellations as they look from the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 天球仪显示出从地球看去的各个星座。
senses.why: instruments that picture the sky borrow the adjective, because they draw the vault as a surface.
senses.whyCN: 把天空画成图面的仪器借用了这个形容词，因为它们把那层穹顶画成了一个曲面。

senses.title: Of navigation by the stars
senses.definition: using the positions of stars and other bodies to find one's way
senses.definitionCN: 利用恒星等天体的位置来确定方位
senses.example: Celestial navigation needs a clear horizon and an accurate clock.
senses.exampleCN: 天文导航需要清晰的地平线和准确的时钟。
senses.why: sailors measured the sky to locate themselves, and the fixed phrase kept the adjective in everyday technical use.
senses.whyCN: 水手通过测量天空来确定自己的位置，这一固定说法把这个形容词留在了日常技术语中。

senses.title: Of the mechanics of bodies
senses.definition: relating to the calculated motions and mutual pulls of bodies in space
senses.definitionCN: 与太空中天体的运动及其相互引力计算有关
senses.example: Celestial mechanics predicts the slow drift of the moon's orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 天体力学预测月球轨道的缓慢漂移。
senses.why: mathematical study of the sky turned the adjective into a technical label for motion under gravity.
senses.whyCN: 对天空的数学研究把这个形容词变成了描述引力下运动的技术标签。

senses.title: Detached from earthly matters
senses.definition: figurative: free of ordinary earthly concerns, almost otherworldly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：摆脱世俗牵挂，近乎不属于人间
senses.example: He kept a celestial calm while the room argued around him.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里众人争吵，他却保持着一种超脱的平静。
senses.why: if heaven is above the earth, a mood can also be lifted clear of earthly noise.
senses.whyCN: 既然天在人间之上，一种心境自然也能被托离尘世的喧闹。

intro.en: Celestial comes through Medieval Latin and Old French from Latin caelestis 'of the sky, heavenly', built on caelum 'sky, heaven'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: celestial 经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入英语，来自拉丁 caelestis「天空的、天上的」，词根为 caelum「天空、天」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caelum meant 'sky, heaven', and was also used for 'climate, region'. A separate caelum meaning 'chisel' exists; whether the two are one word is disputed, so they should not be assumed to be related.
items.cn: caelum 意为「天空、天」，也用于指「气候、地区」。另有一个 caelum 意为「凿子」；两者是否同为一个词尚有争议，不能直接假定同源。

items.en: The adjective caelestis 'heavenly, of the sky' was formed on caelum and used of gods, stars and the heavens.
items.cn: 形容词 caelestis「天上的、天空的」由 caelum 构成，用于神灵、星辰与天界。

items.en: Medieval Latin celestialis and Old French celestial carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, first in religious texts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 celestialis 与古法语 celestial 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带入英语，最初见于宗教文本。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word was applied to the geometry of the sky, giving fixed phrases such as celestial sphere and celestial mechanics.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词被用于描述天空的几何，形成天球、天体力学等固定说法。

items.en: The older religious sense survived in literary writing for anything blissful or supremely beautiful.
items.cn: 较早的宗教义在文学中保留下来，用来形容幸福至极或美到极点的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin origin of caelum is not established, and suggested links to the 'chisel' word or to a reconstructed Italic form remain hypotheses. The earliest English citation is usually placed in the late fourteenth century but is not exact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：caelum 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，把它与「凿子」义或某个重构的意大利语族形式相联系仍属假说。英语最早书证通常放在十四世纪末，但并不确切。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the letters cel- but come from unrelated Latin roots; group two holds words that really do describe the sky or the divine.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 cel- 开头、却来自不同拉丁词根的词；第二组才是真正表示天空或神圣事物的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin celebrare and celeber 'frequented, famous', not from caelum: to mark an occasion with ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 celebrare 与 celeber「常有人来的、著名的」，并非出自 caelum：以仪式庆祝某件事。

entries.definition: From Latin caelebs 'unmarried', a different root: abstaining from marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 caelebs「未婚的」，词根不同：不婚的。

entries.definition: From Latin cellarium 'store-room', from cella 'room': an underground room for storing things.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cellarium「储藏室」，源于 cella「房间」：存放物品的地下室。

entries.definition: From Latin celer 'swift': speed. The shared letters with celestial are coincidence.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 celer「迅捷的」：迅速。与 celestial 相同的字母只是巧合。

entries.definition: The ordinary adjective for the sky or for heaven; celestial is its learned equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指天空或天国的日常形容词；celestial 是它带学术气质的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to astronomy or to the objects it studies; it carries no religious overtone.
entries.definitionCN: 与天文学或天文学研究的对象有关；不带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: Belonging to a god or godlike; celestial means this only in religious or literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 属于神或如神一般；celestial 只在宗教或文学用法中才有这层意思。

entries.definition: Light, airy, as if made of the upper air; celestial is more often about position than texture.
entries.definitionCN: 轻盈飘渺，仿佛由高层空气构成；celestial 更多讲位置，而非质地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: caelum 'sky' plus the relational suffix -ial: the adjective of the sky.
normal.cn: caelum「天空」加上关系形容词后缀 -ial：属于天空的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs celestial, celestially, celestite and celestine.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 celestial、celestially、celestite 与 celestine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: celestial body, celestial mechanics, celestial navigation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：天体、天体力学、天文导航。

normal.en: The same relational ending builds terrestrial and aerial, both adjectives of position.
normal.cn: 同一关系后缀还构成 terrestrial 与 aerial，两者都是表示位置的形容词。

normal.en: Star charts and sextants keep the word at sea and in the observatory.
normal.cn: 星图与六分仪把这个词留在海上和天文台里。

abstract.en: Picture a dome of small lamps switched on above a dark field.
abstract.cn: 想象一片暗地上方点亮一圈小灯，罩成一个穹顶。

abstract.en: Picture a choir heard through a thick stone wall, beautiful and far away.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着一堵厚石墙听见合唱，美好而遥远。

abstract.en: Picture a person so calm that the weather seems to stop at their shoulders.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人静得让天气都在他肩头停住。

examples.en: The celestial sphere is a model, not a real object.
examples.cn: 天球只是一个模型，并非真实存在的物体。

examples.en: Celestial navigation guided the ship across the Pacific.
examples.cn: 天文导航引导这艘船横渡太平洋。

examples.en: The cathedral ceiling was painted to look like a celestial realm.
examples.cn: 教堂穹顶被画成天界的模样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把天空当作一张穹顶：抬头所见的光点，全都属于这张穹顶 → 天空的、天体的、天上的

root: 拉丁 caelum「天空、天」→ caelestis「天空的、天上的」→ 中世纪拉丁 celestialis → 英语 celestial；caelum 更深来源不确定，与「凿子」义的 caelum 是否同词尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upward look: the vault of the sky, the bodies inside it, the heaven beyond it, the beauty that seems to come from there, the instruments that map it, and finally the calm of someone lifted above the earth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次抬头展开：先看天空的穹顶，再看其中的天体，然后是穹顶之外的天国、仿佛来自那里的美、描绘天空的仪器，最后是一个仿佛被托离尘世的人所带的平静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark dome pricked with points of light, with everything above the ground hanging from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色穹顶上布满光点，地面之上的一切都挂在这张穹顶底下。

branches.en: THE VAULT AND ITS MAP: the sky treated as a surface, and the instruments that draw that surface.
branches.cn: 穹顶与图：把天空当作一个曲面，以及描绘这个曲面的仪器。

branches.en: BODIES AND THEIR PATHS: objects in space, the routes found by watching them, and the mathematics of those routes.
branches.cn: 天体与路径：太空中的物体、靠观测找到的路线，以及这些路线的数学。

branches.en: HEAVEN: the same word serves the sky of religion as well as the sky of astronomy.
branches.cn: 天国：同一个词既服务天文学的天空，也服务宗教的天空。

branches.en: BEAUTY: what seems to come from above is felt as perfection.
branches.cn: 美：仿佛来自上方的东西，被人感受为完美。

branches.en: DETACHMENT: a person can be lifted clear of earthly noise, as if into another layer.
branches.cn: 超脱：一个人可以被托离尘世喧闹，仿佛升入另一层。

intro.en: Celestial is a Latin adjective whose root and relational suffix also build a small family, so the word can be read in pieces.
intro.cn: celestial 是一个拉丁形容词，其词根与关系后缀还构成一个小词族，因此可以按语素逐块读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin caelum gives celestial and the mineral name celestite, while the English relational suffix -ial marks an adjective of belonging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 caelum 衍生 celestial 与矿物名 celestite，英语关系后缀 -ial 则表示「属于……的」形容词。

items.example: Caelum also named a region or climate in Latin geography.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁地理学中，caelum 也指地区或气候带。

items.example: Caelestis was used of stars, gods and the heavens.
items.exampleCN: caelestis 用于星辰、神灵与天界。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.meaning: of the sky or of heaven
items.example: The celestial map hung above the telescope.
items.exampleCN: 星空图挂在望远镜上方。

items.meaningCN: 以天空般的方式；超凡地
items.example: The hall was celestially quiet.
items.exampleCN: 大厅静得如同天界。

items.meaning: strontium sulphate, named for its pale blue colour
items.meaningCN: 天青石，硫酸锶矿物，因淡蓝色而得名
items.example: Celestite crystals line the geode.
items.exampleCN: 天青石晶体衬满这个晶洞。

items.meaning: an imaginary sphere on which the stars are projected
items.meaningCN: 把星星投影其上的假想天球
items.example: Astronomers still use the celestial sphere as a coordinate model.
items.exampleCN: 天文学家仍把天球当作坐标模型使用。

items.meaning: the mathematical study of orbital motion
items.meaningCN: 研究轨道运动的数学分支
items.example: Celestial mechanics explains the tides and the seasons.
items.exampleCN: 天体力学解释潮汐与季节。

definition_zh: 天体；地球大气层之外的自然物体（恒星、行星、卫星、小行星、彗星等）
definition_en: a natural object in space beyond the earth's atmosphere, such as a star, planet, moon, asteroid or comet
core_image: 黑绒布上散布着大小不一的发光小球，每颗都沿一条看不见的弧线缓慢移动
scene: 天文台圆顶缓缓打开，观测者把镜筒对准海王星轨道外一个模糊的光点。The telescope tracked a faint celestial body beyond the orbit of Neptune.
sceneCN: 这里 celestial body 指「地球大气层之外的自然物体」（第 1 个义项：天体总称）；句意为望远镜追踪到海王星轨道之外一个微弱的天体。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、轨道弧线、模糊光点、星图。

pos.zh: 天体（可数名词；复数 celestial bodies）

derivatives.zh: 身体的；肉体的（同出 body 词根）

senses.title: A natural object in space
senses.definition: any naturally formed object beyond the earth's atmosphere, considered as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 地球大气层之外自然形成的、被当作一个整体看待的物体
senses.example: Every celestial body follows a path fixed by gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个天体都沿着由引力固定的路径运行。
senses.why: the phrase is the plain cover term: celestial marks its place in the sky, body marks it as one object.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法是最朴素的统称：celestial 标明它在天上，body 标明它是一个单独物体。

senses.title: A star
senses.definition: a celestial body that produces its own light by nuclear fusion
senses.definitionCN: 靠核聚变自行发光的天体
senses.example: A star is a celestial body that shines by its own fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星是靠自身聚变发光的天体。
senses.why: stars were the first celestial bodies to be sorted out, because they shine without help.
senses.whyCN: 恒星是最早被区分出来的一类天体，因为它们无需外物就能发光。

senses.title: A planet
senses.definition: a celestial body that orbits a star, is massive enough to be round, and has cleared its neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行、质量足以呈球形并已清空其轨道附近的天体
senses.example: A planet is a celestial body that orbits a star and has cleared its neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 行星是绕恒星运行并已清空轨道附近的天体。
senses.why: the modern definition turns the old word into a test that a body either passes or fails.
senses.whyCN: 现代定义把这个旧词变成一项检验，天体要么通过，要么不通过。

senses.title: A natural satellite
senses.definition: a celestial body that orbits a planet or a smaller body
senses.definitionCN: 绕行星或更小天体运行的天体
senses.example: The moon is the only natural celestial body that people have visited.
senses.exampleCN: 月球是人类唯一造访过的天然天体。
senses.why: moons were once counted as planets; once they were seen to circle planets, they became satellites among celestial bodies.
senses.whyCN: 卫星一度被算作行星；当人们看出它们绕着行星转，它们就成了天体中的卫星。

senses.title: A minor body
senses.titleCN: 小天体（小行星与彗星等）
senses.definition: a small celestial body such as an asteroid, comet or meteoroid, left over from the formation of a planetary system
senses.definitionCN: 小行星、彗星、流星体等小天体，为行星系形成时的残留物
senses.example: Comets and asteroids are small celestial bodies left over from the early solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星与小行星是早期太阳系遗留下来的小天体。
senses.why: the phrase covers leftovers too small to be round, so it keeps a place for rubble as well as for worlds.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法也涵盖小到无法呈球形的残渣，因此既给世界留位置，也给碎石留位置。

senses.title: A dwarf planet
senses.definition: a round celestial body that orbits a star but has not cleared its neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行、呈球形但未清空轨道附近的天体
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet, a small celestial body in its own class.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星被重新归类为矮行星，自成一类小天体。
senses.why: the dwarf class was created when the planet test was tightened, and the wider phrase absorbed the losers.
senses.whyCN: 当行星的检验标准收紧时，矮行星这一类别被造出来，而更宽泛的天体说法收留了落选者。

senses.title: An exoplanet
senses.definition: a celestial body detected in orbit around another star
senses.definitionCN: 在另一颗恒星周围轨道上被探测到的天体
senses.example: An exoplanet is a celestial body detected around another star.
senses.exampleCN: 系外行星是在另一颗恒星周围探测到的天体。
senses.why: once instruments could see the wobble of distant suns, the phrase extended beyond our own system.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能看见遥远恒星摆动时，这个说法就超出了我们的行星系。

senses.title: An artificial object
senses.definition: a human-made object in orbit, sometimes listed as an artificial celestial body although many catalogues exclude it
senses.definitionCN: 在轨道上运行的人造物体，有时被列为「人造天体」，但许多编目并不把它算入
senses.example: A spacecraft is sometimes listed as an artificial celestial body, though many catalogues exclude it.
senses.exampleCN: 航天器有时被列为「人造天体」，但许多编目将其排除。
senses.why: the extension is a boundary case: the phrase grew in astronomy, and engineers borrowed it for objects they had launched.
senses.whyCN: 这一延伸属于边界情形：这个说法生长于天文学，工程师又借它来指自己发射的物体。

intro.en: The phrase joins Latin caelestis 'heavenly' with English body, a word of Old English origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这一短语把拉丁 caelestis「天上的」与英语本族词 body 组合在一起。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caelestis 'of the sky, heavenly' comes from caelum 'sky, heaven'; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: caelestis「天空的、天上的」来自 caelum「天空、天」；其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Body goes back to Old English bodig 'trunk, chest', the physical frame of a person or animal. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and a suggested link to Old High German botah is only a hypothesis.
items.cn: body 可追溯到古英语 bodig「躯干、胸部」，指人或动物的身体骨架。其更深来源不确定，把它与古高地德语 botah 相联系只是假说。

items.en: English combines the adjective with body to name a distinct physical object; in astronomical writing the phrase is fixed by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语把这个形容词与 body 组合起来，指一个独立可辨的物体；在天文写作中，这一短语在十八世纪固定下来。

items.en: Telescopes and orbital calculations made the phrase the ordinary cover term for stars, planets, moons and smaller objects.
items.cn: 望远镜与轨道计算使这一短语成为恒星、行星、卫星及更小物体的常用统称。

items.en: Spacecraft are sometimes called artificial celestial bodies, though many reference works restrict the phrase to natural objects.
items.cn: 航天器有时被称为「人造天体」，但许多工具书仍把这个说法限于自然物体。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of the compound is recorded, and it becomes common in astronomical writing only in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：这一复合说法的确切首见英语书证未被记录，直到十八、十九世纪它才在天文写作中常见起来。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring phrases that share the word celestial but name a model, a discipline or an instrument; group two holds true alternatives for an object in space.
note.cn: 第一组是同样带 celestial 的相邻说法，但分别指模型、学科或仪器；第二组才是太空中物体的真正近义说法。

entries.definition: An imaginary sphere on which the stars are projected for calculation; it is a coordinate surface, not a physical body.
entries.definitionCN: 为计算而把星星投影其上的假想球面；它是坐标面，不是实体。

entries.definition: The mathematical study of orbital motion; the phrase names a discipline, not a thing in space.
entries.definitionCN: 研究轨道运动的数学分支；这个说法指的是一门学科，而非太空中的东西。

entries.definition: A globe marked with constellations and star positions, used for teaching and navigation.
entries.definitionCN: 标有星座与恒星位置的地球仪式仪器，用于教学与导航。

entries.definition: Fragments of rockets and satellites in orbit; unlike a celestial body, it is not a natural object.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道上的火箭与卫星碎片；与天体不同，它不是自然形成的物体。

entries.definition: The standard technical term for a naturally occurring object in space; it overlaps almost completely with celestial body.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中自然形成的物体的标准技术术语，与 celestial body 几乎完全重合。

entries.definition: The older everyday phrasing, common in religious and popular writing before the technical term spread.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的日常说法，在技术术语普及之前常见于宗教与通俗文字。

entries.definition: A body that orbits a star and has cleared its neighbourhood; it is a hyponym, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 绕恒星运行并已清空轨道附近的天体；它是下位词，而非同义词。

entries.definition: A body that shines by fusion; calling every celestial body a star is the commonest overgeneralisation.
entries.definitionCN: 靠聚变发光的天体；把一切天体都叫作恒星是最常见的过度概括。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin caelestis 'heavenly' plus English body 'one physical object'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 caelestis「天上的」加英语 body「一个物体」。

normal.en: The plural is irregular in the second word: celestial bodies, not celestial bodys.
normal.cn: 复数变化在第二个词上：celestial bodies，而不是 celestial bodys。

normal.en: The phrase covers stars, planets, moons, asteroids, comets, dwarf planets and exoplanets.
normal.cn: 这个说法涵盖恒星、行星、卫星、小行星、彗星、矮行星与系外行星。

normal.en: Synonyms split by register: heavenly body is older and popular, astronomical object is technical.
normal.cn: 近义词按语体分开：heavenly body 较旧且通俗，astronomical object 偏技术。

normal.en: The boundary case is the spacecraft, sometimes called an artificial celestial body.
normal.cn: 边界情形是航天器，有时被称为「人造天体」。

abstract.en: Picture marbles of different sizes rolling on a dark cloth, each on its own invisible arc.
abstract.cn: 想象大小不一的弹珠在深色布上滚动，各自沿一条看不见的弧线。

abstract.en: Picture a bonfire seen from a hill: one point of light that makes its own glow.
abstract.cn: 想象从山丘上看见一堆篝火：一个自己发光的点。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that has circled the same lamp for billions of years.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头绕着同一盏灯转了几十亿年。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every known celestial body in the survey area.
examples.cn: 该星表列出了巡天区域内所有已知天体。

examples.en: Gravity holds every celestial body in its orbit.
examples.cn: 引力把每一个天体都约束在轨道上。

examples.en: A new celestial body was announced after three nights of observation.
examples.cn: 经过三夜观测，一个新的天体被公布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 天体就是「天上的一整个物体」：不管它是恒星、行星还是碎石，只要在天空里自成一个整体，就叫天体

root: 拉丁 caelestis「天上的」+ 英语 body「物体」；caelestis 出自 caelum「天空」，body 出自古英语 bodig「躯干」，两者更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses sort the same phrase by what the object is: the general cover term, then a star, a planet, a moon, a leftover rock, a dwarf planet, a world around another sun, and finally a human-made boundary case.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按「这个物体是什么」把同一个说法分类：先是总称，再是恒星、行星、卫星、残余碎石、矮行星、绕另一颗太阳的世界，最后是人造的边界情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one distinct object hanging in the dark, held on a path by gravity.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个独立物体悬在黑暗中，被引力牵在一条路径上。

branches.en: THE COVER TERM: first of all the phrase simply names one natural object out in space.
branches.cn: 统称：这个说法首先只指太空中一个自然物体。

branches.en: OWN LIGHT: a star is the case where the object makes its own glow.
branches.cn: 自发光：恒星是物体自己发光的那个情形。

branches.en: ORBIT AND CLEARANCE: a planet adds both a stellar orbit and a swept path.
branches.cn: 绕行与清空：行星同时要求绕恒星运行与清空轨道。

branches.en: SMALLER CLASSES: moons circle planets, rubble never became round, and dwarf planets fail the clearance test.
branches.cn: 更小的类别：卫星绕行星，碎石从未成球，矮行星未通过清空检验。

branches.en: BEYOND THE OLD FRAME: the phrase stretches to worlds around other suns and, at the edge, to objects people built.
branches.cn: 超出旧框架：这个说法延伸到绕其他恒星的世界，并在边缘延伸到人造物体。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin adjective and an English noun, so its two halves belong to two different layers of the language.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个拉丁形容词和一个英语名词构成，两半分别属于语言的两个不同层次。

latinIntro.en: Latin caelum and caelestis supply the first half, while body and its relatives come from Old English; the astronomical compounds are built on the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 前半由拉丁 caelum 与 caelestis 提供，body 及其同族词来自古英语；天文复合词则都建立在英语名词 body 上。

items.meaning: of the sky or of heaven
items.example: A celestial map hung beside the telescope.
items.exampleCN: 望远镜旁挂着一张星空图。

items.meaning: a physical object; the frame of a person or animal
items.example: Every body in the simulation has mass.
items.exampleCN: 模拟中的每个物体都有质量。

items.example: The telescope tracked a faint celestial body.
items.exampleCN: 望远镜追踪到一个微弱的天体。

items.example: Older books speak of the heavenly bodies.
items.exampleCN: 较早的书里说「天上的物体」。

items.example: Stars are projected onto the celestial sphere.
items.exampleCN: 恒星被投影到天球上。

items.example: Celestial mechanics predicts the eclipse to the minute.
items.exampleCN: 天体力学把食的时刻预测到分钟。

items.example: Bodily motion differs from orbital motion.
items.exampleCN: 身体运动与轨道运动不同。

items.example: A coordinate point is bodiless by design.
items.exampleCN: 坐标点在设计上就是无形的。

definition_zh: 气候的；与一个地区长期天气状况有关的
definition_en: relating to the long-term weather conditions of a region rather than to a single day's weather
core_image: 同一条山坡上，几十年的温度曲线被压成一条缓慢起伏的平滑长线
scene: 山谷里的气象站保存了几十年的温度与降水记录。Long-term records show a climatic shift toward warmer winters.
sceneCN: 这里 climatic 指「与长期气候状况有关的」（第 1 个义项：气候的）；句意为长期记录显示气候正朝更暖的冬季偏移。图中可辨识物件：百叶箱、记录纸、温度曲线、山谷。

pos.zh: 气候的；与气候有关的
由气候造成的；气候性的

senses.title: Relating to climate
senses.definition: relating to the weather conditions that a region has over many years
senses.definitionCN: 与一个地区多年来的天气状况有关
senses.example: Climatic conditions decide which crops ripen in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 气候条件决定这个山谷里哪些作物能够成熟。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the noun climate to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词「气候」挂到它所描述的事物上。

senses.title: Caused by climate
senses.definition: produced or driven by long-term weather patterns rather than by a single event
senses.definitionCN: 由长期天气模式造成，而非由单次事件造成
senses.example: The canyon's shape is partly a climatic effect of dry centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这条峡谷的形态部分是数百年干旱造成的气候性结果。
senses.why: once climate names a cause, the adjective can mark an effect that follows from it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦气候被当作原因，这个形容词就能标示由它产生的后果。

senses.title: Of a climatic zone
senses.definition: relating to one of the broad belts into which the earth is divided by climate
senses.definitionCN: 与按气候把地球划分成的某个大带有关
senses.example: The map colours each climatic zone a different shade.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用不同深浅的颜色标出每一个气候带。
senses.why: the oldest sense of the root is a belt or zone, so the adjective still marks those belts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最早的意思就是「带、区域」，因此这个形容词仍用来标示这些带。

senses.title: Of climate records
senses.definition: relating to the measured series of temperature, rainfall and other weather data
senses.definitionCN: 与温度、降水等长期观测数据序列有关
senses.example: Climatic records from the station go back to the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个台站的气候记录可追溯到十九世纪。
senses.why: data are called climatic when they describe climate rather than a day's weather.
senses.whyCN: 当数据描述的是气候而非某一天的天气时，就被称作气候数据。

senses.title: Of biological adaptation
senses.definition: relating to the adjustments by which living things cope with a particular climate
senses.definitionCN: 与生物为适应特定气候而做出的调整有关
senses.example: Thick fur is a climatic adaptation found in many mountain mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 厚毛是许多山地哺乳动物身上可见的一种气候适应。
senses.why: ecology borrowed the adjective to label traits shaped by long-term weather.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个形容词，用来标示被长期天气塑造的性状。

senses.title: Of extremes
senses.definition: relating to unusually severe weather that a climate makes more or less likely
senses.definitionCN: 与某种气候使之更易或更不易发生的异常剧烈天气有关
senses.example: Climatic extremes such as heat waves now appear in the risk models.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪这类极端气候事件如今进入了风险模型。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from typical conditions to the rare events those conditions produce.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从典型状况转指这些状况所催生的罕见事件。

senses.title: Of variability
senses.definition: relating to how much climate varies from year to year or decade to decade
senses.definitionCN: 与气候在年际或年代际间的变化幅度有关
senses.example: Climatic variability makes a single dry year hard to interpret.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变率使得单独一个干旱年份难以解读。
senses.why: a climate is not a constant, and the adjective covers its range of change.
senses.whyCN: 气候并非常量，这个形容词涵盖它的变化幅度。

senses.title: Of projections and models
senses.definition: relating to calculated future climates produced by computer models
senses.definitionCN: 与计算机模式算出的未来气候有关
senses.example: Climatic projections disagree mainly about the next fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 气候预估的分歧主要集中在未来五十年。
senses.why: the newest sense comes from modelling, where the adjective marks a computed rather than observed climate.
senses.whyCN: 最新的义项来自建模，此时这个形容词标示的是算出的而非观测到的气候。

intro.en: Climatic is climate plus the Latin-derived suffix -ic, and climate goes back through Latin and Greek to a word for a slope or a zone. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climatic 是 climate 加拉丁来源的后缀 -ic；climate 则经拉丁语与希腊语追溯到表示「斜坡、地带」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek klima meant 'slope, inclination', then 'zone of the earth', because the inhabited zones were pictured as bands tilted from the equator toward the poles. It comes from klimein 'to lean'.
items.cn: 希腊 klima 意为「斜坡、倾斜」，后指「地带」，因为当时把人居地带想象成从赤道向两极倾斜的条带。它出自 klimein「倾斜」。

items.en: Latin clima, climat- took the Greek word into geographical writing, where it named a belt of the earth fixed by latitude.
items.cn: 拉丁 clima（词干 climat-）把希腊词带入地理写作，用来指由纬度确定的地球条带。

items.en: Old French climat and Latin climat- gave English climate in the late fourteenth century, first as a geographical belt and later as the typical weather of a region.
items.cn: 古法语 climat 与拉丁词干 climat- 在十四世纪末带来英语 climate，最初指地理上的带，后来指一个地区的典型天气。

items.en: The adjective climatic was formed on climate with the suffix -ic in the nineteenth century, once climate had acquired its modern weather meaning.
items.cn: 形容词 climatic 在十九世纪由 climate 加后缀 -ic 构成，此时 climate 已获得现代天气义。

items.en: Climatic then spread into compounds such as climatic zone, climatic change and climatic data.
items.cn: climatic 随后扩展到气候带、气候变迁、气候资料等固定说法中。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of climatic is recorded, and it is usually placed in the nineteenth century; its formation from climate is transparent.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：climatic 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常放在十九世纪；它由 climate 构成，来路清楚。

note.en: Group one holds the word most often mistaken for climatic, plus near neighbours from different roots; group two holds adjectives that genuinely describe weather or climate.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误作 climatic 的词，以及来自不同词根的相邻词；第二组才是真正描述天气或气候的形容词。

entries.definition: From Greek klimax 'ladder' through climax: relating to the most intense point of a story or event. It has nothing to do with climate.
entries.definitionCN: 经 climax 来自希腊 klimax「梯子」：指故事或事件最紧张的高点。与气候无关。

entries.definition: From Greek klimaktēr 'rung of a ladder': a critical period or turning point, also used in physiology.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 klimaktēr「梯级」：指关键时期或转折点，也用于生理学。

entries.definition: A poetic shortening of climate, still used for a region and its weather; it shares the root but not the technical range.
entries.definitionCN: climate 的诗体缩略形式，仍指地区及其天气；词根相同，技术用法范围不同。

entries.definition: The descriptive mapping of climates, as opposed to climatology, which studies causes and processes.
entries.definitionCN: 对气候的描述性制图，与研究成因与过程的气候学相对。

entries.definition: Relating to weather and its observation; a single storm is meteorological, a shift over decades is climatic.
entries.definitionCN: 与天气及其观测有关；一场风暴是气象的，数十年的偏移才是气候的。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole surroundings, of which climate is one part; it is wider and less precise.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个周围环境有关，气候只是其中一部分；范围更宽，也更不精确。

entries.definition: Relating to the cycle of seasons within a year, not to multi-year climate.
entries.definitionCN: 与一年内的季节循环有关，而非多年气候。

entries.definition: A plain compound for anything caused by day-to-day weather; it lacks the long timescale of climatic.
entries.definitionCN: 指由日常天气造成的任何事情的朴素复合说法；缺少 climatic 的长时间尺度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek klima 'slope, zone' gives climate, and climate plus -ic gives climatic.
normal.cn: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」给出 climate，climate 加 -ic 得到 climatic。

normal.en: The family runs climate, climatic, climatically, climatology, climatologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 climate、climatic、climatically、climatology、climatologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the two registers: climatic change and climatic zone.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分两种语域：气候变迁与气候带。

normal.en: The classic trap is climactic, which belongs to climax and means the peak of a story.
normal.cn: 经典陷阱是 climactic，它属于 climax，指故事的高潮。

normal.en: A climate is measured in decades; a weather report is measured in hours.
normal.cn: 气候以十年计，天气报告以小时计。

abstract.en: Picture a single smooth line drawn through thousands of jagged daily readings.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平滑的长线穿过成千上万个锯齿状的每日读数。

abstract.en: Picture a broad band of colour painted across a continent.
abstract.cn: 想象一整条宽色带横涂在大陆上。

abstract.en: Picture a slope so gentle that a whole life fits on it without a bump.
abstract.cn: 想象一道坡缓得能放下人的一生而不见一个凸起。

examples.en: Climatic zones shift slowly as the ocean currents change.
examples.cn: 随着洋流改变，气候带缓慢移动。

examples.en: The study separates climatic effects from human ones.
examples.cn: 这项研究把气候造成的影响与人为影响分开。

examples.en: Climatic data from the ice core cover ten thousand years.
examples.cn: 来自冰芯的气候资料覆盖一万年。

dict_mnemonic.text: climate 是「气候」，加 -ic 就成「气候的」；记住它不是 climactic（高潮的），两者只差一个字母却完全不同源

root: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」（出自 klimein「倾斜」）→ 拉丁 clima（词干 climat-）→ 英语 climate → climate + -ic → climatic；与 climax 来的 climactic 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one long timescale: the general adjective, then effects, belts, records, adaptations, extremes, variability and finally computed futures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都沿着同一个长时间尺度展开：先是一般形容词，再是后果、地带、记录、适应、极端事件、变化幅度，最后是算出的未来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one smooth line drawn through thousands of jagged daily readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条平滑的线穿过成千上万个锯齿状的每日读数。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE BELT: the adjective names a region's long-run weather and the broad zones drawn from it.
branches.cn: 模式与地带：这个形容词指一个地区的长期天气，以及据此画出的宽大地带。

branches.en: FROM CONDITION TO EVENT: a climate both shapes ordinary conditions and makes rare extremes more likely.
branches.cn: 从状况到事件：气候既塑造日常状况，也使罕见的极端事件更易发生。

branches.en: THE RECORD: measurement turns a pattern into a series that can be read.
branches.cn: 记录：测量把一种模式变成可读取的序列。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE: living things adjust to a climate, and the adjective labels those traits.
branches.cn: 回应：生物适应气候，这个形容词就标示这些性状。

branches.en: RANGE AND FORECAST: the pattern is never constant, and its future is now computed.
branches.cn: 幅度与预报：这种模式从不是常量，而它的未来如今由计算给出。

intro.en: Climatic is a noun plus a suffix, and both the noun and the suffix have long histories that also build many related words.
intro.cn: climatic 是一个名词加一个后缀，名词与后缀都有很长的历史，也各自构成许多相关词。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima and Latin clima give climate; the suffix -ic goes back to Greek -ikos through Latin -icus and marks a relation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 与拉丁 clima 给出 climate；后缀 -ic 经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos，表示某种关系。

items.example: The word began as a description of tilt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初描述的是倾斜。

items.example: Latin geography listed seven climata.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁地理学列出七个地带。

items.meaning: the long-term weather of a region
items.example: The valley has a dry climate.
items.exampleCN: 这个山谷气候干燥。

items.example: Climatic change reshaped the coast.
items.exampleCN: 气候变迁重塑了海岸。

items.example: The two sites are climatically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地点在气候上相似。

items.example: Climatology compares decades, not days.

items.exampleCN: 一位气候学家解读了冰芯。

definition_en: the scientific study of climates: how they form, vary over time and space, and affect living things

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies climates as long-term systems
senses.definitionCN: 把气候当作长期系统来研究的科学分支
senses.example: Climatology asks why two regions at the same latitude differ.
senses.exampleCN: 气候学追问：为何同纬度的两个地区气候不同。
senses.why: the suffix for 'study' attached to climate names the discipline as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 表示「研究」的后缀加在 climate 上，指的就是这门学科整体。

senses.title: Physical climatology
senses.definition: the branch that explains climate through radiation, heat, moisture and circulation
senses.definitionCN: 用辐射、热量、水汽与环流来解释气候的分支
senses.example: Physical climatology models how the ocean stores heat.
senses.exampleCN: 物理气候学研究海洋如何储存热量。
senses.why: physics supplies the mechanisms, so the discipline splits off a branch named for them.
senses.whyCN: 物理学提供机制，于是学科分出以它命名的一支。

senses.title: Regional climatology
senses.definition: the branch that describes and compares the climates of particular regions
senses.definitionCN: 描述并比较特定地区气候的分支
senses.example: Regional climatology maps the monsoon belt in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 区域气候学详细绘制季风带。
senses.why: a region is the natural unit of description, so the field grew a branch named for it.
senses.whyCN: 地区是描述气候的自然单位，于是学科长出一支以它命名的分枝。

senses.title: Historical climatology
senses.titleCN: 古气候学与历史气候学
senses.definition: the branch that reconstructs past climates from ice, sediment, tree rings and written records
senses.definitionCN: 从冰芯、沉积、年轮与文献重建过去气候的分支
senses.example: Historical climatology reads old harvest logs for frost dates.
senses.exampleCN: 历史气候学从旧收成记录里读出霜期。
senses.why: a climate has a history, so the discipline grew a branch that looks backward.
senses.whyCN: 气候有自己的历史，于是学科长出一支回望过去的枝。

senses.title: Applied climatology
senses.definition: the use of climate knowledge in farming, building, health and energy planning
senses.definitionCN: 把气候知识用于农业、建筑、健康与能源规划
senses.example: Applied climatology advises growers on planting dates.
senses.exampleCN: 应用气候学为种植者提供播期建议。
senses.why: users needed answers rather than descriptions, so a branch was named for its use.
senses.whyCN: 使用者要的是答案而非描述，于是出现一支以用途命名的分枝。

senses.title: Statistical climatology and modelling
senses.titleCN: 统计气候学与气候建模
senses.definition: the branch that summarises climate statistically and simulates it with computers
senses.definitionCN: 用统计方法概括气候并用计算机模拟的分支
senses.example: Statistical climatology separates a trend from ordinary noise.
senses.exampleCN: 统计气候学把趋势与普通噪声分开。
senses.why: climate is a distribution rather than a single event, so numerical summary became a branch of its own.
senses.whyCN: 气候是一个分布而非单次事件，于是数值概括自成一门分枝。

senses.title: The climatology of a place
senses.definition: a counted noun: the documented climate of one place, often as a long series of averages
senses.definitionCN: 可数用法：某一个地方有记录的气候，常表现为一长串平均值
senses.example: The station published a climatology of the upper valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该站发布了上游山谷的气候志。
senses.why: one place's full file of averages is a countable product, so the discipline name gained a countable use.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方整套的平均记录是可数的成果，于是学科名多出一个可数用法。

senses.title: A long-term average state
senses.definition: technical: the average condition used as a baseline in forecasting and modelling
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：预报与建模中作为基准的长期平均状况
senses.example: Models compare each season with the modelled climatology.
senses.exampleCN: 模式把每个季节与模式算出的气候平均态作比较。
senses.why: forecasting needs a baseline, and the discipline's name became the word for that baseline.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要一个基准，于是学科之名变成了这个基准的叫法。

intro.en: Climatology joins climate with the Greek-derived suffix -logy 'study'. The word belongs to the scientific vocabulary of the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climatology 由 climate 与希腊来源的后缀 -logy「研究」组合而成，属于十九世纪的科学词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek klima 'slope, zone' named the belts of the earth fixed by latitude; it comes from klimein 'to lean'.
items.cn: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」指由纬度确定的地球条带，出自 klimein「倾斜」。

items.en: Greek -logia 'account, study' comes from logos 'word, reason, account'; Latin -logia passed it into the learned languages of Europe.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia「记述、研究」出自 logos「言词、理性、说明」；拉丁 -logia 把它传入欧洲的学术语言。

items.en: English climate arrived in the late fourteenth century from Old French and Latin, first as a geographical belt and later as a region's weather.
items.cn: 英语 climate 在十四世纪末经古法语与拉丁语进入，先指地理上的带，后指一个地区的天气。

items.en: Climatology appears in the nineteenth century as the name for the systematic study of climates, beside the older descriptive term climatography.
items.cn: climatology 在十九世纪出现，成为系统研究气候的学科名，与较早的描述性术语 climatography 并存。

items.en: In the twentieth century the field split into physical, regional, statistical and historical branches, and the word came to cover computer modelling as well.
items.cn: 二十世纪这门学科分成物理、区域、统计与历史等分支，这个词也开始涵盖计算机建模。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first citation is agreed, and the term is usually dated to the early nineteenth century. Its formation, climate plus the suffix for 'study', is transparent.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：没有公认的确切首见书证，这个词通常被定在十九世纪初。它的构成——climate 加表示「研究」的后缀——则一目了然。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike names from neighbouring fields and subfields; group two holds the wider or narrower sciences that are often confused with climatology.
note.cn: 第一组是邻近领域与分支中形似的名称；第二组是常与气候学混淆的、范围更宽或更窄的学科。

entries.definition: The descriptive mapping and tabulation of climates; -graphy means writing or drawing, while -logy means reasoned study.
entries.definitionCN: 对气候的描述性制图与制表；-graphy 意为书写描绘，-logy 意为有理据的研究。

entries.definition: The reconstruction of ancient climates; it is a branch of climatology, not a rival term.
entries.definitionCN: 对古代气候的重建；它是气候学的分支，而非对立名称。

entries.definition: The study of climate as it affects living things; again a branch built with a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 研究气候对生物影响的学科；同样是以前缀构成的分支。

entries.definition: The adjective of climatology; it describes data or averages rather than the discipline itself.
entries.definitionCN: climatology 的形容词，描述数据或平均值，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: The science of the atmosphere and of weather over short periods; climatology studies the long average of that weather.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气与短期天气的科学；气候学研究这些天气的长期平均。

entries.definition: The everyday and policy name for the same field, often used where climatology sounds academic.
entries.definitionCN: 同一领域的日常与政策名称，常在气候学听起来太学术的场合使用。

entries.definition: The broad study of the atmosphere, of which climatology is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 对大气层的广泛研究，气候学只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: The study of the earth's surface and its places; climate is only one of its subjects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球表面及其地方的综合学科；气候只是其主题之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: climate plus -logy, the suffix for a reasoned study.
normal.cn: climate 加 -logy，即表示有理据研究的后缀。

normal.en: The family runs climatology, climatologist, climatological, paleoclimatology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 climatology、climatologist、climatological、paleoclimatology。

normal.en: The oldest sister term is climatography, which describes rather than explains.
normal.cn: 最早的姊妹术语是 climatography，它描述而不解释。

normal.en: The discipline is counted in decades and centuries, unlike meteorology.
normal.cn: 这门学科以十年与百年为尺度，与气象学不同。

normal.en: Branches are marked by prefixes: physical, regional, historical, applied, statistical.
normal.cn: 分支由前缀标出：物理、区域、历史、应用、统计。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of isotherms cutting a continent into belts.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙等温线把大陆切成条带。

abstract.en: Picture a single average drawn through a century of storms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平均值穿过一个世纪的风暴。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every drawer holds one year of weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每个抽屉装着一年的天气。

examples.en: Climatology explains why the two coasts differ despite equal latitude.
examples.cn: 气候学解释了为何两片海岸纬度相同却气候不同。

examples.en: She studied climatology before moving into policy.
examples.cn: 她在进入政策领域之前学的是气候学。

examples.en: The paper compares observed rainfall with the model climatology.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把观测降水与模式的气候平均态作比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: climate 是气候，-logy 是「学科」：研究气候的学问就是气候学；记住它研究的是几十年的平均，而不是明天下不下雨

root: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」→ 拉丁 clima → 英语 climate；再加希腊 -logia「研究」→ climatology；与 meteorology（气象学）分工不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one science outward: the discipline itself, then its physical, regional, historical, applied and statistical branches, then a place's documented climate, and finally the average used as a baseline.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一门学科向外铺开：先是学科本身，再是物理、区域、历史、应用与统计各分支，然后是一个地方有记录的气候，最后是作为基准的平均态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of isotherms cutting a continent into belts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一墙等温线把大陆切成一条条带。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the suffix for study turns climate into a discipline.
branches.cn: 整体：表示研究的后缀把气候变成一门学科。

branches.en: PHYSICS: radiation, heat and circulation explain the pattern.
branches.cn: 物理：辐射、热量与环流解释这种模式。

branches.en: SPACE AND TIME: one branch compares regions, another reconstructs past climates.
branches.cn: 空间与时间：一支比较地区，一支重建过去的气候。

branches.en: USE AND NUMBER: knowledge is applied to farming and building, and summarised by statistics and models.
branches.cn: 应用与数字：知识被用于农业与建筑，又被统计与模式概括。

branches.en: THE LOCAL RECORD AND THE BASELINE: a place's counted climate, and the average a forecast measures against.
branches.cn: 地方记录与基准：一个地方可数的气候，以及预报用来对照的平均值。

intro.en: Climatology is a compound of a noun and a suffix of Greek origin, and each half has its own family of English words.
intro.cn: climatology 由一个名词与一个希腊来源的后缀复合而成，两半各自都有英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima and Latin clima give climate; Greek -logia and Latin -logia give the second half, which also builds biology, geology and meteorology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 与拉丁 clima 给出 climate；希腊 -logia 与拉丁 -logia 给出后半，也构成 biology、geology、meteorology 等词。

items.example: The word described a tilt before it described a region.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先描述倾斜，后描述地区。

items.example: The suffix names a field of knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为一片知识领域命名。

items.meaning: the long-term weather of a region
items.example: The climate of the plateau is severe.
items.exampleCN: 高原的气候严酷。

items.example: Climatology compares centuries of records.
items.exampleCN: 气候学比较数百年的记录。

items.example: A climatologist joined the field team.
items.exampleCN: 一位气候学家加入了野外队伍。

items.example: The climatological average hides the storm.
items.exampleCN: 气候平均值掩盖了那场风暴。

items.example: Paleoclimatology reads ice cores.
items.exampleCN: 古气候学解读冰芯。

items.example: Bioclimatology maps mosquito ranges.
items.exampleCN: 生物气候学绘制蚊虫分布范围。

items.example: Meteorology forecast the storm; climatology counted it.
items.exampleCN: 气象学预报了风暴，气候学把它计入统计。

definition_zh: 气候学家；研究气候的科学家
definition_en: a scientist who studies climates, their patterns and how they change over long periods
core_image: 一个人站在高原站的仪器旁，手里夹着一叠跨越几十年的观测表
scene: 一位研究者长期驻守高原站，整理积雪与气温的观测表。A climatologist compared fifty winters of snowfall records.
sceneCN: 这里 climatologist 指「研究气候的科学家」（第 1 个义项：气候学家）；句意为一位气候学家比较了五十个冬季的降雪记录。图中可辨识物件：高原气象站、观测表、积雪尺、保温服。

pos.zh: 气候学家（可数名词；复数 climatologists）

senses.title: A climate scientist
senses.definition: a scientist whose subject is climate rather than day-to-day weather
senses.definitionCN: 以气候而非日常天气为研究对象的科学家
senses.example: A climatologist was asked to explain the thirty-year trend.
senses.exampleCN: 一位气候学家被请来解释这三十年的趋势。
senses.why: the person suffix added to the discipline names whoever practises it.
senses.whyCN: 加在学科名上的人物后缀，指从事这门学科的人。

senses.title: An observational climatologist
senses.definition: one who works from long instrument records and station networks
senses.definitionCN: 依靠长期仪器记录与台站网开展工作的研究者
senses.example: An observational climatologist checked the station series for gaps.
senses.exampleCN: 一位观测型气候学家检查了台站序列中的缺测。
senses.why: the branch is named for its method: instruments and networks supply the raw series.
senses.whyCN: 这一支以方法命名：仪器与台站网提供原始序列。

senses.title: A modelling climatologist
senses.definition: one who builds and runs computer models of the climate system
senses.definitionCN: 构建并运行气候系统计算机模式的研究者
senses.example: A modelling climatologist tested how the ocean responds.
senses.exampleCN: 一位建模型气候学家检验了海洋如何响应。
senses.why: the same discipline also works on simulated climates, so its practitioners split by method.
senses.whyCN: 同一学科也处理模拟气候，于是从业者按方法分工。

senses.title: A paleoclimatologist
senses.definition: one who reconstructs climates from ice, sediment, rings and old documents
senses.definitionCN: 从冰芯、沉积、年轮与旧文献重建气候的研究者
senses.example: A paleoclimatologist dated the cold spell from lake mud.
senses.exampleCN: 一位古气候学家依据湖底淤泥确定了这次寒冷期的年代。
senses.why: climates older than instruments need proxies, and a specialist grew up around those proxies.
senses.whyCN: 比仪器更古老的气候需要替代指标，围绕这些指标就长出一类专家。

senses.title: A regional specialist
senses.definition: one whose expertise is the climate of a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 专门研究某一地区气候的研究者
senses.example: A regional climatologist knows the monsoon's local timing.
senses.exampleCN: 一位区域气候学家熟悉季风在当地的时序。
senses.why: monsoon timing differs from valley to valley, so local knowledge became its own expertise.
senses.whyCN: 季风时序各地不同，因此地方知识本身成了专长。

senses.title: An applied climatologist
senses.definition: one who turns climate knowledge into advice for farming, building or health
senses.definitionCN: 把气候知识转化为农业、建筑或健康建议的研究者
senses.example: An applied climatologist advised the city on heat planning.
senses.exampleCN: 一位应用气候学家就城市高温规划提供建议。
senses.why: users need decisions rather than papers, and the role is named for that translation.
senses.whyCN: 使用者需要决定而非论文，这个角色就因这种转化而得名。

senses.title: A climate services adviser
senses.definition: one who works in an agency producing outlooks and climate services for government or industry
senses.definitionCN: 在机构中为政府或行业制作气候展望与服务的研究者
senses.example: The agency's climatologist briefed the water authority.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构的气候学家向水务部门做了简报。
senses.why: climate knowledge reaches decisions through agencies, and the title follows the service it provides.
senses.whyCN: 气候知识通过机构抵达决策，头衔就随所供的服务而来。

senses.title: A teacher or communicator
senses.titleCN: 气候学的教师与解说者
senses.definition: one who teaches climatology or explains it to the public
senses.definitionCN: 教授气候学或向公众解释气候学的人
senses.example: The climatologist's column made the jet stream readable.
senses.exampleCN: 这位气候学家的专栏把急流讲得通俗易懂。
senses.why: a discipline also lives through teaching and explanation, so the same title covers that work.
senses.whyCN: 学科也靠教学与解释存活，因此同一头衔也涵盖这项工作。

intro.en: Climatologist joins climatology with the Greek-derived person suffix -ist. The word is a nineteenth-century scientific formation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climatologist 由 climatology 加希腊来源的人物后缀 -ist 构成，是十九世纪的科学构词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek klima 'slope, zone' gave Latin clima and English climate.
items.cn: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」给出拉丁 clima 与英语 climate。

items.en: The suffix for 'study' comes from logos 'word, reason', through Latin -logia.
items.cn: 表示「研究」的后缀出自 logos「言词、理性」，经拉丁 -logia 传入。

items.en: Greek -istēs named a person who does something; Latin -ista and French -iste carried it into English -ist.
items.cn: 希腊 -istēs 指从事某事的人；拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 把它带入英语的 -ist。

items.en: Climatology appears in the nineteenth century, and climatologist follows as the name of its practitioner.
items.cn: 气候学在十九世纪出现，气候学家这一称呼随之而来，指从事该学科的人。

items.en: In the twentieth century the role split into observational, modelling, regional and applied posts, and climate services gave it a public face.
items.cn: 二十世纪这一角色分成观测、建模、区域与应用等岗位，气候服务又给它一张面向公众的脸。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of climatologist is recorded, and it is usually dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：climatologist 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常定在十九世纪。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring job titles that share the ending or the field but differ in scope; group two holds real alternatives for a climate specialist.
note.cn: 第一组是结尾相同或领域相邻、但范围不同的职称；第二组才是气候专家的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: The adjective of the discipline, not a person; it describes data, averages and services.
entries.definitionCN: 学科的形容词，不指人；它描述数据、平均值与服务。

entries.definition: A specialist in ancient climates only, one branch rather than the whole discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究古代气候的专家，属一个分支而非整个学科。

entries.definition: A specialist in weather and forecasting over hours and days, not in multi-decade climate.
entries.definitionCN: 研究以小时和天计的天气与预报的专家，而非数十年尺度的气候。

entries.definition: A rarely used feminine form built on the Spanish and Italian pattern; standard English uses the same form for both sexes.
entries.definitionCN: 按西班牙语与意大利语模式构成的罕见阴性形式；标准英语男女同形。

entries.definition: The everyday and policy term for the same profession; it avoids the rarer discipline name.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业的日常与政策用语，避免了较少见的学科名。

entries.definition: The weather counterpart; the two often work in the same agency but on different timescales.
entries.definitionCN: 天气方面的对应职业；两者常在同一机构工作，但时间尺度不同。

entries.definition: A broader title covering chemistry, physics and dynamics of the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的头衔，涵盖大气的化学、物理与动力学。

entries.definition: A specialist in places and surfaces, for whom climate is one subject among many.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地方与地表的专家，气候只是其众多主题之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: climatology plus -ist: the person who practises the discipline.
normal.cn: climatology 加 -ist：从事这门学科的人。

normal.en: The family runs climatology, climatologist, climatological, paleoclimatologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 climatology、climatologist、climatological、paleoclimatologist。

normal.en: The job title marks its timescale: a climatologist counts decades, a meteorologist counts days.
normal.cn: 这个职称标出时间尺度：气候学家数十年，气象学家数天。

normal.en: Agency posts add adjectives: observational, modelling, regional, applied.
normal.cn: 机构岗位加形容词：观测型、建模型、区域、应用。

normal.en: Climate services put the specialist in front of water boards and city planners.
normal.cn: 气候服务把这类专家带到水务部门与城市规划者面前。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding a stack of tables that covers more years than their own life.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人抱着一叠比自己一生还长的观测表。

abstract.en: Picture a single station on a high plateau, visited every morning for forty years.
abstract.cn: 想象高原上一座台站，四十年来每天早上都有人到访。

abstract.en: Picture a model on a screen beside a real valley, both showing the same slow curve.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的模式与真实山谷并排，显示同一条缓慢曲线。

examples.en: The climatologist compared snowfall records across five decades.
examples.cn: 这位气候学家比较了跨越五十年的降雪记录。

examples.en: A climatologist warned that one wet year proves little.
examples.cn: 一位气候学家提醒说，单独一个湿润年份说明不了什么。

examples.en: The team hired a climatologist to review the long-range outlook.
examples.cn: 团队聘请了一位气候学家来审阅长期展望。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practitioner outward: the general title, then observation, modelling, ancient climates, regional expertise, applied advice, climate services and teaching.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一位从业者向外展开：先是总称，再是观测、建模、古气候、区域专长、应用建议、气候服务与教学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person at a high station holding decades of tables.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在高原台站，手里拿着几十年的观测表。

branches.en: THE TITLE: the person suffix turns the discipline into a profession.
branches.cn: 头衔：人物后缀把学科变成一个职业。

branches.en: TWO METHODS: one reads instruments, the other runs models.
branches.cn: 两种方法：一种读仪器，一种跑模式。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: the same craft applied to climates before records began.
branches.cn: 深时：同一手艺用于记录开始之前的气候。

branches.en: PLACE AND PRACTICE: regional knowledge turned into advice for growers and builders.
branches.cn: 地方与实践：区域知识转化为给种植者与建筑者的建议。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC FACE: outlooks for agencies, and explanation for everyone else.
branches.cn: 公众面孔：为机构做展望，也为其他人做解释。

intro.en: Climatologist is a stack of three pieces: the noun climate, the suffix for a field of study, and the suffix for a person.
intro.cn: climatologist 由三层叠成：名词 climate、表示研究领域的后缀，以及表示人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin clima supplies the base, Greek -logia the field, and Greek -istēs through Latin -ista the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 clima 提供基底，希腊 -logia 提供领域，希腊 -istēs 经拉丁 -ista 提供人物后缀。

definition_zh: 气象学；研究大气与天气现象的学科
definition_en: the science that studies the atmosphere, its phenomena and the weather they produce
core_image: 值班室里，卫星云图、雷达回波与地面观测表叠在同一张桌面上
scene: 清晨的预报中心里，值班员把卫星云图与地面观测叠在一起看。Modern meteorology combines satellite images with surface observations.
sceneCN: 这里 meteorology 指「研究大气与天气的学科」（第 1 个义项：气象学总称）；句意为现代气象学把卫星图像与地面观测结合起来。图中可辨识物件：卫星云图、雷达屏、地面观测表、值班台。

pos.zh: 气象学（不可数名词，指学科）
气象业务；气象服务（机构或工作层面的用法）

senses.title: The science of the atmosphere
senses.definition: the science of the atmosphere and of the weather it produces
senses.definitionCN: 研究大气及其产生的天气的科学
senses.example: Meteorology explains both a single storm and the calm after it.
senses.exampleCN: 气象学既解释一场风暴，也解释风暴之后的平静。
senses.why: the suffix for a reasoned study attached to the Greek word for things high in the air names the field.
senses.whyCN: 表示有理据研究的前缀加在希腊语「高空之物」上，就成了这门学科的名字。

senses.title: Weather observation and forecasting
senses.definition: the working practice of watching the weather and issuing forecasts
senses.definitionCN: 观察天气并发布预报的实际工作
senses.example: Meteorology in this office means three forecasts a day.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个办公室里，气象工作意味着每天三次预报。
senses.why: a science that predicts has a daily product, and the same word names the service as well as the study.
senses.whyCN: 一门会预测的科学有每日产出，于是同一个词既指研究，也指业务。

senses.title: Physical meteorology
senses.definition: the branch that studies radiation, cloud physics and the thermodynamics of the air
senses.definitionCN: 研究辐射、云物理与空气热力学的分支
senses.example: Physical meteorology measures how ice crystals grow in a cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 物理气象学测量冰晶在云中如何生长。
senses.why: physics supplies the mechanisms of cloud, radiation and heat.
senses.whyCN: 物理学提供云、辐射与热量的机制。

senses.title: Dynamic meteorology
senses.definition: the branch that applies fluid mechanics to the motions of the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把流体力学用于大气运动的分支
senses.example: Dynamic meteorology treats the jet stream as a rotating fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 动力气象学把急流当作旋转流体来处理。
senses.why: fluid mechanics supplies the equations for moving air.
senses.whyCN: 流体力学提供运动空气的方程。

senses.title: Aviation and marine meteorology
senses.definition: the applied branches that serve aircraft and ships with route-specific warnings
senses.definitionCN: 为飞机与船舶提供航线专项警报的应用分支
senses.example: Aviation meteorology issues warnings for icing at altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 航空气象学发布高空结冰警报。
senses.why: users on a route need warnings tied to their path, so applied branches formed.
senses.whyCN: 航线上的使用者需要与路径相连的警报，于是形成应用分支。

senses.title: Agricultural meteorology
senses.definition: the applied branch that links weather to crops, livestock and soil
senses.definitionCN: 把天气与作物、牲畜和土壤联系起来的应用分支
senses.example: Agricultural meteorology timed the irrigation after the dry spell.
senses.exampleCN: 农业气象学在干旱期之后安排了灌溉时机。
senses.why: growers need weather turned into timing, and the branch is named for that conversion.
senses.whyCN: 种植者需要把天气变成时机，这一支就因这种转化而得名。

senses.title: The meteorological service
senses.definition: the agency or service that carries out observation and forecasting for the public
senses.definitionCN: 为公众开展观测与预报的机构或服务
senses.example: The national meteorology office upgraded its radar network.
senses.exampleCN: 国家气象部门升级了雷达网。
senses.why: institutions take the name of the science, because their whole work is that science applied.
senses.whyCN: 机构以学科之名命名，因为它们的全部工作就是这门学科的应用。

senses.title: The older sense: high phenomena
senses.definition: historical: the study of things high in the air, including shooting stars, before astronomy split off
senses.definitionCN: 历史义：在天文学分离出去之前，对高空之物（包括流星）的研究
senses.example: Early meteorology dealt with comets as well as clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的气象学既处理云，也处理彗星。
senses.why: the Greek word covered everything raised above the earth, so the old sense was far wider than weather.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原词涵盖一切被举离地面的东西，因此旧义远比天气宽。

intro.en: Meteorology comes from Greek meteōrologia 'discussion of things high in the air', a compound of meteōron and the suffix for a reasoned account. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meteorology 来自希腊 meteōrologia「对高空之物的论述」，由 meteōron 与表示有理据记述的后缀复合而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek meteōron 'thing high up' is built from meta- 'beyond, up' and aeirein 'to lift, raise'. It named anything seen high in the air, including shooting stars.
items.cn: 希腊 meteōron「高处之物」由 meta-「超出、向上」与 aeirein「举起、抬高」构成，指一切在高空可见之物，包括流星。

items.en: Meteōrologia meant 'discussion of celestial and atmospheric phenomena', essentially astronomy in the ancient sense.
items.cn: meteōrologia 意为「对天象与大气现象的论述」，在古代意义上基本等同于天文学。

items.en: English meteorology appears in the early seventeenth century with that broad sense: the study of things high above the earth.
items.cn: 英语 meteorology 在十七世纪初出现，带着这一宽泛含义：研究地球上方高处之物。

items.en: As astronomy became a separate science, meteorology narrowed to the atmosphere and its weather, and by the nineteenth century it meant the science of weather.
items.cn: 随着天文学独立成科，气象学收窄到大气及其天气，到十九世纪已指天气的科学。

items.en: The field now covers observation, theory and forecasting, and divides into physical and dynamical branches.
items.cn: 这门学科如今涵盖观测、理论与预报，并分成物理与动力两大分支。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is usually placed in the 1610s but is not exact, and the pre-Greek origin of aeirein is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语最早书证通常放在十七世纪一十年代，但并不确切；aeirein 在希腊语之前的来源也未得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to meteorology but belong to other roots; group two holds neighbouring sciences and services.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近气象学、却属于其他词根的词；第二组是相邻的学科与服务。

entries.definition: From Greek metron 'measure': the science of measurement. A single letter separates it from meteorology.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 metron「度量」：测量科学。它与气象学只差一个字母。

entries.definition: A streak of light from a body burning in the air, or the body itself; it is one subject of meteorology, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 物体在大气中燃烧产生的光迹，或该物体本身；它是气象学的研究对象之一，而非学科。

entries.definition: The study of meteorites, which belongs to planetary science rather than to weather.
entries.definitionCN: 研究陨石的学科，属于行星科学而非天气研究。

entries.definition: A small body in space before it enters the atmosphere; the word names an object, not a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 进入大气之前的小天体；这个词指物体，不指学科。

entries.definition: The study of climates over decades and centuries; meteorology handles hours and days.
entries.definitionCN: 研究数十年至数百年的气候；气象学处理小时与天。

entries.definition: The broad study of the atmosphere, including chemistry and upper-air physics as well as weather.
entries.definitionCN: 对大气的广泛研究，除天气外还包括化学与高空物理。

entries.definition: The operational activity of predicting weather; it is the public face of meteorology.
entries.definitionCN: 预测天气的业务活动，是气象学面向公众的一面。

entries.definition: The physics and chemistry of the upper atmosphere; it is a narrow branch, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 高层大气的物理与化学；它是狭窄分支，并非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek meteōron 'thing high up' plus the suffix for a reasoned study.
normal.cn: 希腊 meteōron「高处之物」加表示有理据研究后缀。

normal.en: The family runs meteorology, meteorologist, meteorological, meteor, meteorite.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 meteorology、meteorologist、meteorological、meteor、meteorite。

normal.en: The trap is metrology, the science of measurement, which differs by one letter.
normal.cn: 陷阱是 metrology（测量科学），只差一个字母。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark branches: synoptic, physical, dynamic, agricultural, aviation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：天气学、物理、动力、农业、航空。

normal.en: The old sense covered shooting stars, which is why meteor is a sky object, not a weather word.
normal.cn: 旧义涵盖流星，所以 meteor 是天空物体，而非天气词。

abstract.cn: 想象桌上叠着三张图：云图、雷达图与台站表。

abstract.cn: 想象从云朵画向海岸的一条箭头。

dict_mnemonic.text: meteor 是「高空之物」，加上 -logy（学科）：研究高空之物的学问 → 气象学；注意别和测量科学 metrology 混淆

root: 希腊 meteōron「高处之物」（meta-「超出」+ aeirein「举起」）+ 希腊 -logia「研究」→ meteorology；aeirein 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one science from its old breadth to its modern branches: the field, its forecast work, its physical and dynamical halves, its aviation and farm applications, its public agency, and finally the older study of everything high in the air.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一门学科从旧日的宽广走向现代的分支：学科本身、预报业务、物理与动力两半、航空与农业应用、面向公众的机构，最后是旧日对一切高空之物的研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloud, a radar echo and a station table laid on the same desk.

branches.en: FROM HIGH THINGS TO WEATHER: the old wide sense and the modern field share the same name.
branches.cn: 从高空之物到天气：旧日宽泛义与现代学科共用同一个名字。

branches.en: THE DAILY PRODUCT AND THE AGENCY: a predicting science becomes a service and an office.
branches.cn: 每日产出与机构：一门会预测的科学变成了服务与部门。

branches.en: PHYSICS: radiation and cloud physics explain how the air makes its weather.
branches.cn: 物理：辐射与云物理说明空气如何造出天气。

branches.en: DYNAMICS: fluid mechanics explains how the air moves.
branches.cn: 动力：流体力学说明空气如何运动。

branches.en: TWO USERS: aircraft need warnings, farms need timing.
branches.cn: 两类使用者：飞机要警报，农田要时机。

intro.en: Meteorology is a Greek compound whose pieces also build meteor, meteorite and the names of many sciences.
intro.cn: meteorology 是一个希腊复合词，其构件还构成 meteor、meteorite 以及许多学科名。

latinIntro.en: Greek meteōron and -logia passed into modern Latin as meteorologia, and the same pieces appear in Latinized scientific names.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meteōron 与 -logia 作为 meteorologia 进入现代拉丁语，同样的构件也出现在拉丁化的科学名称中。

senses.title: Relating to meteorology
senses.definition: relating to meteorology as a science or to its methods
senses.definitionCN: 与作为学科的气象学或其方法有关

senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the discipline to the thing it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把学科挂到它所描述的事物上。

senses.title: Of observation

senses.why: observation is the base of the science, and the adjective marks its instruments and records.
