senses.title: Of forecasting
senses.definition: relating to the issuing of weather forecasts and warnings
senses.definitionCN: 与发布天气预报和警报有关
senses.example: A meteorological warning closed the harbour at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 一份气象警报让港口在正午关闭。
senses.why: forecasting is the science aimed at tomorrow, so the adjective marks its warnings.
senses.whyCN: 预报是面向明天的科学，这个形容词标示它的警报。

senses.title: Of weather conditions
senses.titleCN: 气象条件的；天气造成的
senses.definition: caused by or dependent on the actual weather at a place and time
senses.definitionCN: 由某地某时的实际天气造成或取决于它
senses.example: The delay was purely meteorological, not mechanical.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误纯属天气原因，而非机械故障。
senses.why: when a cause lies in the weather, the adjective shifts from the science to its object.
senses.whyCN: 当原因出在天气本身，这个形容词就从学科转向它的对象。

senses.title: Of platforms and instruments
senses.titleCN: 气象卫星与雷达平台的
senses.definition: relating to satellites, radar and other platforms that carry weather instruments
senses.definitionCN: 与搭载气象仪器的卫星、雷达等平台有关
senses.example: The meteorological satellite sent a new image every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗气象卫星每小时传回一张新图。
senses.why: instruments ride on platforms, and the adjective follows them into orbit.
senses.whyCN: 仪器搭载在平台上，这个形容词便跟着它们进入轨道。

senses.title: Of hazards
senses.definition: relating to severe weather that threatens life or property
senses.definitionCN: 与威胁生命或财产的剧烈天气有关
senses.example: Meteorological hazards were mapped along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海地区标出了气象灾害风险。
senses.why: a hazard is weather strong enough to demand a warning.
senses.whyCN: 灾害就是强到必须发出警报的天气。

senses.title: Of institutions
senses.definition: relating to agencies and organisations that coordinate weather work
senses.definitionCN: 与协调气象工作的机构与组织有关
senses.example: The meteorological organisation publishes the global normals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个气象组织发布全球气候平均值。
senses.why: collective work takes the adjective into the name of the body.
senses.whyCN: 集体工作把这个形容词带进机构名称。

senses.title: Technical sense
senses.definition: technical: used in the precise vocabulary of atmospheric measurement and theory
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：用于大气测量与理论的精确术语中
senses.example: Meteorological visibility is measured in metres.
senses.exampleCN: 气象能见度以米为单位测量。
senses.why: measurement needs precise terms, and the adjective supplies them.
senses.whyCN: 测量需要精确术语，这个形容词提供这些术语。

intro.en: Meteorological is meteorology plus the adjective suffix -ical, which goes back through Latin to Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meteorological 是 meteorology 加形容词后缀 -ical，后者经拉丁语追溯到希腊语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meteōron 'thing high up' comes from meta- 'beyond, up' and aeirein 'to lift'; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: meteōron「高处之物」出自 meta-「超出、向上」与 aeirein「举起」；其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Greek -ikos formed adjectives of relation; Latin -icus carried the suffix into the learned vocabulary of Europe.
items.cn: 希腊 -ikos 构成表示关系的形容词；拉丁 -icus 把这个后缀带入欧洲的学术词汇。

items.en: English -ical is the fuller form of -ic, often used when a noun in -ology or -ics stands behind the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 -ical 是 -ic 的完整形式，当形容词背后是 -ology 或 -ics 结尾的名词时常用。

items.en: Meteorological settles as the standard adjective in the nineteenth century, as weather services and observatories expand.
items.cn: 随着气象服务与观测台扩充，meteorological 在十九世纪成为标准形容词。

items.en: The word entered the names of international bodies and services in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词进入国际机构与气象服务的名称。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of meteorological is recorded, and it is usually placed in the eighteenth or early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：meteorological 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常放在十八世纪或十九世纪初。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that differ from meteorological by a letter or a root; group two holds adjectives that really describe weather or climate.
note.cn: 第一组是与 meteorological 相差一个字母或词根的形容词；第二组才是真正描述天气或气候的形容词。

entries.definition: A shorter, rare form of the same adjective, mostly found in older scientific prose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较短罕见形式，多见于较早的科学文字。

entries.definition: Relating to metrology, the science of measurement; the root is Greek metron, not meteōron.
entries.definitionCN: 与测量科学有关；词根是希腊 metron，而非 meteōron。

entries.definition: Relating to meteorites and to meteoritics; it concerns space rocks, not the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 与陨石及陨石学有关；讲的是太空岩石，不是大气。

entries.definition: Relating to method; the resemblance is only in the long ending.
entries.definitionCN: 与方法有关；相似之处只在长长的词尾。

entries.definition: Relating to climate over decades; meteorological refers to weather and its measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 与数十年尺度的气候有关；meteorological 指天气及其测量。

entries.definition: A plain everyday compound for anything caused by weather; meteorological is its technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指由天气造成的任何事的日常复合说法；meteorological 是其技术对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to the atmosphere as a physical medium; meteorological usually implies observation and forecasting.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为物理介质的大气有关；meteorological 通常含观测与预报之意。

entries.definition: Relating to a barometer and to pressure measurement; it is narrower than meteorological.
entries.definitionCN: 与气压计及气压测量有关；范围比 meteorological 窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: meteorology plus -ical, the adjective suffix of a discipline.
normal.cn: meteorology 加 -ical，即学科的形容词后缀。

normal.en: The family runs meteorology, meteorological, meteorologist, meteorologically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 meteorology、meteorological、meteorologist、meteorologically。

normal.en: The trap is metrological, which belongs to measurement, not weather.
normal.cn: 陷阱是 metrological，它属于测量，不属于天气。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the hardware: meteorological station, meteorological satellite, meteorological radar.
normal.cn: 固定搭配点名硬件：气象站、气象卫星、气象雷达。

normal.en: Institutional names carry the word: a meteorological organisation or service.
normal.cn: 机构名也带这个词：气象组织或气象服务。

abstract.en: Picture a small white box on a lawn, its instruments turning all night.
abstract.cn: 想象草坪上一只白色百叶箱，仪器整夜转动。

abstract.en: Picture a satellite drawing a spiral of cloud from above.
abstract.cn: 想象卫星从高处画出一圈螺旋云带。

abstract.en: Picture a warning strip pasted across a harbour gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一张警报条贴在港口大门上。

examples.en: The meteorological station has run since the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 这座气象站从十九世纪运行至今。

examples.en: Meteorological conditions grounded the small aircraft.
examples.cn: 气象条件使小型飞机停飞。

examples.en: The agency issues meteorological warnings for the coast.
examples.cn: 该机构为沿海发布气象警报。

dict_mnemonic.text: meteorology 是气象学，-ical 是形容词后缀：气象学的、气象的；注意别写成 metrological（测量学的）

root: 希腊 meteōron「高处之物」+ -logia「研究」→ meteorology；再加 -ical（经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos）→ meteorological。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective through its uses: the discipline, its instruments, its forecasts, the actual weather, its satellites, its hazards, its agencies and its technical vocabulary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词的用法展开：学科、仪器、预报、实际天气、卫星、灾害、机构与技术术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white instrument box on a lawn, turning through the night.
core.cn: 核心意象：草坪上一只白色仪器箱，整夜转动。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS VOCABULARY: the adjective marks both the field and its precise terms.
branches.cn: 学科与术语：这个形容词既标学科，也标精确术语。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: stations on the ground and satellites above both supply the numbers.
branches.cn: 测量：地面台站与天上卫星都提供数字。

branches.en: WARNING: a forecast and a hazard notice are the same knowledge aimed at action.
branches.cn: 警报：预报与灾害通告是同一知识对准行动。

branches.en: THE CAUSE ITSELF: sometimes the weather, not the science, is what the adjective points to.
branches.cn: 原因本身：有时这个形容词指向的是天气，而不是学科。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: collective work takes the adjective into its name.
branches.cn: 机构：集体工作把这个形容词带进名称。

intro.en: Meteorological is a long adjective built from a Greek compound plus two layers of suffix, and each layer also appears in other scientific words.
intro.cn: meteorological 是一个长形容词，由希腊复合词加两层后缀构成，每一层也出现在其他科学词中。

latinIntro.en: Greek meteōron plus -logia gives the noun, and -ikos through Latin -icus gives the adjective ending; modern Latin writes meteorologia and meteorologicus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meteōron 加 -logia 构成名词，-ikos 经拉丁 -icus 构成形容词词尾；现代拉丁写作 meteorologia 与 meteorologicus。

items.example: The compound begins with the sky.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词从天空开始。

items.example: The suffix names the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为领域命名。

items.example: The ending turns the field into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成形容词。

items.example: Meteorology supplies the daily map.
items.exampleCN: 气象学提供每日天气图。

items.example: Meteorological data fill the archive.
items.exampleCN: 气象数据填满档案。

items.example: The two sites are meteorologically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地点在气象上不同。

items.meaning: a rare variant of the adjective
items.example: Older papers used the meteorologic form.
items.exampleCN: 较早的论文用这一短式。

items.example: A meteorologist wrote the warning.
items.exampleCN: 一位气象学家写了这份警报。

items.example: The meteor lit the ridge for a second.
items.exampleCN: 流星把山脊照亮了一瞬。

definition_zh: 气象学家；从事气象观测、研究或预报的专家
definition_en: a scientist who studies the atmosphere or who prepares weather observations and forecasts
core_image: 值班室里，一个人盯着雷达回波，手指沿着雨带边缘移动
scene: 值班室里，一个人盯着雷达回波，判断雨带是否会转向城区。The meteorologist expected the rain band to reach the coast by evening.
sceneCN: 这里 meteorologist 指「从事气象工作的专家」（第 1 个义项：气象学家）；句意为这位气象学家预计雨带将在傍晚抵达海岸。图中可辨识物件：雷达回波、雨带、值班台、时钟。

pos.zh: 气象学家；气象工作者（可数名词；复数 meteorologists）

senses.title: A weather scientist
senses.definition: a scientist whose subject is the atmosphere and its weather
senses.definitionCN: 以大气及其天气为研究对象的科学家
senses.example: The meteorologist explained why the fog formed in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这位气象学家解释了雾为何在山谷里形成。
senses.why: the person suffix added to the discipline names whoever practises it.
senses.whyCN: 加在学科名上的人物后缀，指从事这门学科的人。

senses.title: An operational forecaster
senses.definition: one whose daily work is to issue forecasts and warnings on a shift
senses.definitionCN: 日常工作是在轮班中发布预报与警报的人
senses.example: The meteorologist on duty updated the coastal warning.
senses.exampleCN: 值班气象员更新了沿海警报。
senses.why: the shift produces forecasts, and the title follows the shift.
senses.whyCN: 轮班产出预报，头衔就跟着轮班走。

senses.title: A research meteorologist
senses.definition: one who studies atmospheric processes rather than issuing routine forecasts
senses.definitionCN: 研究大气过程、而非发布日常预报的研究者
senses.example: A research meteorologist modelled how hail grows.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究型气象学家模拟了冰雹如何生长。
senses.why: the same craft also asks how processes work, not only what happens next.
senses.whyCN: 同一门手艺也追问过程如何运作，而不只问接下来会怎样。

senses.title: A broadcast meteorologist
senses.definition: one who presents forecasts on radio or television and explains them to the public
senses.definitionCN: 在广播或电视上呈现预报并向公众解释的人
senses.example: The broadcast meteorologist kept the map simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这位广播气象播报员把图讲得很简单。
senses.why: a forecast needs a voice, and broadcasting created a version of the role.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要一张嘴，广播就造出这个角色的一种版本。

senses.title: An aviation meteorologist
senses.definition: one who briefs pilots on winds, icing and visibility along a route
senses.definitionCN: 向飞行员简报航线上的风、结冰与能见度的人
senses.example: An aviation meteorologist warned of icing over the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一位航空气象员警告山口上空有结冰。
senses.why: flying needs route-specific warnings, so a specialism formed.
senses.whyCN: 飞行需要航线专项警报，于是形成一个专长。

senses.title: A military meteorologist
senses.definition: one who supplies weather support to military operations
senses.definitionCN: 为军事行动提供气象保障的人
senses.example: The military meteorologist timed the exercise around the front.
senses.exampleCN: 这位军事气象员围绕锋面安排了演习时间。
senses.why: operations need weather support, and the military kept its own specialists.
senses.whyCN: 行动需要气象保障，军队便保留自己的专家。

senses.title: A climate-adjacent specialist
senses.titleCN: 与气候研究交叉的专家
senses.definition: one whose atmospheric work overlaps with climate science and long-range outlooks
senses.definitionCN: 大气工作与气候科学及长期展望交叉的研究者
senses.example: The meteorologist worked with climatologists on the seasonal outlook.
senses.exampleCN: 这位气象学家与气候学家合作做季节展望。
senses.why: weather and climate meet at the seasonal scale, so the roles overlap.
senses.whyCN: 天气与气候在季节尺度上相遇，两个角色便重叠。

senses.title: The older sense: a sky phenomenon scholar
senses.titleCN: 旧义：研究高空现象的人
senses.definition: historical: a person who studied things high in the air, including meteors
senses.definitionCN: 历史义：研究高空之物（包括流星）的人
senses.example: An early meteorologist catalogued comets and winds alike.
senses.exampleCN: 早期这类学者把彗星与风一并记录。
senses.why: before the science split, anyone who watched the sky bore the same title.
senses.whyCN: 在学科分开之前，任何观天的人都带同一头衔。

intro.en: Meteorologist joins meteorology with the Greek-derived person suffix -ist. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: meteorologist 由 meteorology 加希腊来源的人物后缀 -ist 构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meteōron 'thing high up' was built on meta- 'up' and aeirein 'to lift'; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: meteōron「高处之物」由 meta-「向上」与 aeirein「举起」构成；其更深来源不确定。

items.en: The suffix for a reasoned study comes from logos 'word, reason', through Latin -logia.
items.cn: 表示有理据研究的前缀出自 logos「言词、理性」，经拉丁 -logia 传入。

items.en: Greek -istēs named a person who does something; Latin -ista and French -iste carried it into English -ist.
items.cn: 希腊 -istēs 指从事某事的人；拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 把它带入英语 -ist。

items.en: The title appears in the nineteenth century, as weather services begin to employ trained staff.
items.cn: 这一职称在十九世纪出现，正值气象服务开始雇用受过训练的人员。

items.en: In the twentieth century the role divided into forecast desks, research groups, aviation briefings, broadcasting and military support.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个角色分成预报台、研究组、航空简报、广播与军事保障。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of meteorologist is recorded, and it is usually dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：meteorologist 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常定在十九世纪。

note.en: Group one holds titles that look like meteorologist but belong elsewhere; group two holds real alternatives for the same profession.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 meteorologist、实则属于其他领域的职称；第二组才是同一职业的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: A specialist in measurement, from Greek metron; not a weather scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究测量的专家，词根为希腊 metron；不是气象学家。

entries.definition: A specialist in meteorites, a branch of planetary science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究陨石的专家，属行星科学分支。

entries.definition: An older word for the same profession, now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 同一职业的较旧称呼，现已罕见。

entries.definition: The adjective, not the person; it describes data and stations.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，不指人；它描述数据与台站。

entries.definition: The everyday title for the operational side of the job; a meteorologist may also do research.
entries.definitionCN: 该职业业务一侧的日常称谓；气象学家也可能做研究。

entries.definition: An informal and older word, most often for a broadcast presenter.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的非正式说法，多指广播播报员。

entries.definition: A specialist in climates over decades, not in this week's weather.
entries.definitionCN: 研究数十年尺度气候的专家，而非本周天气。

entries.definition: A broader title covering atmospheric chemistry and physics as well as weather.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽泛的头衔，除天气外还涵盖大气化学与物理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: meteorology plus -ist: the person who practises the science.
normal.cn: meteorology 加 -ist：从事这门科学的人。

normal.en: The family runs meteorology, meteorologist, meteorological, meteor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 meteorology、meteorologist、meteorological、meteor。

normal.en: The trap is metrologist, the measurement specialist.
normal.cn: 陷阱是 metrologist，即测量专家。

normal.en: Job titles take prefixes: broadcast, aviation, research, military, agricultural.
normal.cn: 职称带前缀：广播、航空、研究、军事、农业。

normal.en: The operational product is a forecast; the research product is a paper.
normal.cn: 业务产品是预报，研究产品是论文。

abstract.en: Picture a person tracing a rain band with one finger on a glowing screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用一根手指在发亮的屏幕上描出雨带。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone in one hand and a chart in the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一手拿话筒，一手拿图表。

abstract.en: Picture a pilot and a forecaster reading the same wind profile.
abstract.cn: 想象飞行员与预报员读着同一份风廓线。

examples.en: The meteorologist on duty issued the storm warning.
examples.cn: 值班气象学家发布了风暴警报。

examples.en: A meteorologist briefed the pilots before take-off.
examples.cn: 一位气象学家在起飞前向飞行员做简报。

examples.en: The broadcast meteorologist explained the cold front in one sentence.
examples.cn: 广播气象播报员用一句话解释了冷锋。

dict_mnemonic.text: meteor 是高空之物，-logy 是学科，-ist 是从业者：研究天气的人 → 气象学家；别与测量专家 metrologist 混了

root: 希腊 meteōron「高处之物」+ -logia「研究」→ meteorology；再加希腊 -istēs（经拉丁 -ista）的人物后缀 → meteorologist。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practitioner through the job: the general title, then the shift forecaster, the researcher, the broadcaster, the aviation and military posts, the climate overlap and the older sky scholar.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一位从业者的工作展开：总称、值班预报员、研究者、播报员、航空与军事岗位、与气候研究的交叉，以及旧日的高空现象学者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person tracing a rain band on a glowing screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人发亮的屏幕上描出一条雨带。

branches.en: THE TITLE: the person suffix turns meteorology into a job.
branches.cn: 头衔：人物后缀把气象学变成一个职业。

branches.en: THE SHIFT: forecasts and warnings are produced on the clock.
branches.cn: 值班：预报与警报按时按点产出。

branches.en: THE RESEARCH SIDE: process studies and seasonal outlooks overlap with climate work.
branches.cn: 研究一侧：过程研究与季节展望同气候工作交叉。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCES: the public, pilots and commanders each need a different briefing.
branches.cn: 受众：公众、飞行员与指挥官各需不同的简报。

branches.en: THE OLDER ROLE: the same title once covered anyone who watched the sky.
branches.cn: 较旧的角色：同一头衔曾涵盖一切观天的人。

intro.en: Meteorologist is a stack of three pieces: the sky word, the suffix for a field, and the suffix for a person.
intro.cn: meteorologist 由三层叠成：表示天空的词、表示领域的后缀，以及表示人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek meteōron supplies the base, -logia the field, and -istēs through Latin -ista the person.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meteōron 提供基底，-logia 提供领域，-istēs 经拉丁 -ista 提供人物后缀。

items.example: The base word names the sky.
items.exampleCN: 基础词指天空。

items.example: It marks a field.
items.exampleCN: 它标示一个领域。

items.example: It turns the field into a title.
items.exampleCN: 它把领域变成职称。

items.example: Meteorology explains the front.
items.exampleCN: 气象学解释这条锋面。

items.example: A meteorologist read the radar.
items.exampleCN: 一位气象学家解读雷达。

items.example: Meteorological data were archived.
items.exampleCN: 气象数据被归档。

items.example: A meteor crossed the valley.
items.exampleCN: 一颗流星划过山谷。

items.meaning: a rock that reached the ground

items.exampleCN: 这块陨石保存在博物馆里。

items.example: An agrometeorologist timed the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 一位农业气象学家安排收获时机。

definition_en: the envelope of gases around a planet; the air in a place; the mood that surrounds an event; also a unit of pressure
core_image: 登山者站在雪线之上，天空蓝得发黑，每走一步都要停下来喘气
scene: 登山者站在雪线之上，天空蓝得发黑，呼吸变得短促。At this altitude the atmosphere holds far less oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 atmosphere 指「行星周围的气体包层」（第 1 个义项：大气层）；句意为在这个海拔，大气含氧量少得多。图中可辨识物件：雪线、登山者、氧气瓶、深蓝天空。

pos.zh: 大气层；大气；空气
气氛；氛围；（技术用法）大气压单位

senses.title: The gas envelope of a planet
senses.definition: the layer of gases held by gravity around a planet or other body
senses.definitionCN: 被行星或其他天体的引力束缚住的气体层
senses.example: The atmosphere protects the surface from most small meteors.
senses.exampleCN: 大气层保护地表免受大多数小流星撞击。
senses.why: atmos named vapour and sphaira named ball, so the word pictured a ball of vapour around a body.
senses.whyCN: atmos 指水汽，sphaira 指球，因此这个词描绘的是包住天体的一个汽球。

senses.title: The air of a place
senses.definition: the air itself, considered as the medium in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 把空气本身看作某个场所中的介质
senses.example: The atmosphere in the cave was cold and still.
senses.exampleCN: 洞穴里的空气又冷又静。
senses.why: once the envelope is named, the same word can simply mean the air inside it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那层包层有了名字，同一个词也能直接指包层里的空气。

senses.title: The air of a room
senses.definition: the quality of the air in an enclosed space, especially its warmth, dampness or smell
senses.definitionCN: 封闭空间中空气的质地，尤指温度、湿度或气味
senses.example: The old library had a dry, papery atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧图书馆的空气干燥，带纸张的气味。
senses.why: enclosed air takes on a character, and the word shifts from substance to sensed quality.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的空气带上性格，这个词就从物质转向可感的质地。

senses.title: A surrounding mood
senses.definition: the feeling or mood produced by a place, event or group of people
senses.definitionCN: 由场所、事件或人群产生的感觉或情绪
senses.example: A quiet atmosphere settled over the hall before the results.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布前，大厅里笼罩着一种安静的气氛。
senses.why: a mood surrounds people the way air surrounds a room, so the physical word became social.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像空气包围房间一样包围人，于是物理词变成了社会词。

senses.title: An artistic tone
senses.definition: the prevailing tone or feeling of a work of art, music or writing
senses.definitionCN: 艺术、音乐或文学作品中占主导的调子或感觉
senses.example: The film builds its atmosphere through rain and long silences.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片靠雨水与长久的沉默营造基调。
senses.why: tone is something a work carries, so the word for surrounding air serves art too.
senses.whyCN: 调子是作品携带的东西，于是表示环绕空气的词也服务艺术。

senses.title: The envelope of another body
senses.definition: the gaseous envelope of a planet, moon or star other than the earth
senses.definitionCN: 地球以外行星、卫星或恒星的气体包层
senses.example: Titan's atmosphere is thicker than the moon's.
senses.exampleCN: 土卫六的大气比月球的大气厚。
senses.why: the same physical word applies to any body that holds gas.
senses.whyCN: 同一个物理词适用于任何能束缚气体的天体。

senses.title: A unit of pressure
senses.definition: technical: a unit of pressure equal to the average sea-level pressure of the earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：等于地球海平面平均气压的压强单位
senses.example: The chamber was pumped down to a tenth of an atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这个舱被抽到十分之一个大气压。
senses.why: the envelope became a measuring stick, so its name turned into a unit.
senses.whyCN: 那层包层成了量尺，它的名字也就变成了单位。

senses.title: An enveloping influence
senses.definition: figurative: an influence or condition that seems to surround and press on everything
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：仿佛包围并压在一切事物上的影响或状况
senses.example: An atmosphere of suspicion followed the inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，一种猜疑的氛围笼罩下来。
senses.why: whatever surrounds a group behaves like air, and the word extends to abstract pressure.
senses.whyCN: 包围一群人的东西行为像空气，这个词就延伸到抽象的压力。

intro.en: Atmosphere is a Latinized Greek compound of atmos 'vapour' and sphaira 'sphere', coined in seventeenth-century science. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: atmosphere 是拉丁化的希腊复合词，由 atmos「水汽」与 sphaira「球」构成，在十七世纪科学中造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek atmos 'vapour' and sphaira 'ball' were joined in seventeenth-century Latin as atmosphaera for the envelope of air around a body. The deeper origin of atmos is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊 atmos「水汽」与 sphaira「球」在十七世纪的拉丁语中组合成 atmosphaera，指包住天体的空气层。atmos 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: English atmosphere entered in the 1630s from the Latinized form, first as a scientific term.
items.cn: 英语 atmosphere 在十七世纪三十年代由拉丁化形式进入，最初是科学术语。

items.en: By the late eighteenth century atmosphere was used for a surrounding mental or social influence, hence the mood of a place.
items.cn: 到十八世纪晚期，这个词已用于指包围人的心理或社会影响，因此有「场所气氛」之义。

items.en: In the nineteenth century atmosphere also became the name of a pressure unit, the standard atmosphere.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个词又成为一个压强单位的名称，即标准大气压。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of atmos and first date): the pre-Greek source of atmos is unknown, and the earliest English use is dated only approximately to the 1630s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（atmos 的来源与首见年代）：atmos 在希腊语之前的来源不明，英语最早书证也只能约略定在十七世纪三十年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same pieces that are not the noun atmosphere; group two holds words for air, mood and surrounding influence.
note.cn: 第一组是同样构件构成、却不是名词 atmosphere 的形式；第二组是表示空气、气氛与环绕影响的词。

entries.definition: The adjective of atmosphere; it describes layers, pressure and moods rather than naming the envelope.
entries.definitionCN: atmosphere 的形容词，描述层次、气压与氛围，而不指那层包层本身。

entries.definition: Radio noise from electrical activity in the air, and also deliberate mood effects in art.
entries.definitionCN: 由大气中放电造成的无线电噪声，也指艺术中刻意营造的氛围效果。

entries.definition: A geometrical ball; it supplies the shape in the compound but names no air.
entries.definitionCN: 几何球体；它只提供复合词中的形状，并不指空气。

entries.definition: A rare word for the airy envelope, built on Greek aēr instead of atmos.
entries.definitionCN: 指空气包层的罕见词，用希腊 aēr 而非 atmos 构成。

entries.definition: The plain word for the mixture of gases; it names what the atmosphere is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 指混合气体的朴素词，说明大气由什么构成。

entries.definition: The feeling of a place, without the physical sense; it is the closest synonym for sense four.
entries.definitionCN: 场所给人的感觉，不含物理义；是第四个义项最接近的同义词。

entries.definition: A temporary state of feeling, personal or collective; narrower than the social atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或集体的暂时情绪状态；比社会性的 atmosphere 窄。

entries.definition: A quality that seems to radiate from a person or place; more mysterious than atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 仿佛从人或地方散发出的气质；比 atmosphere 更神秘。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek atmos 'vapour' plus sphaira 'sphere': a ball of vapour around a body.
normal.cn: 希腊 atmos「水汽」加 sphaira「球」：包住天体的汽球。

normal.en: The family runs atmosphere, atmospheric, atmospherically, atmospherics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 atmosphere、atmospheric、atmospherically、atmospherics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: upper atmosphere, friendly atmosphere, one atmosphere.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：高层大气、友好的气氛、一个大气压。

normal.en: Astronomy applies it to other worlds: the atmosphere of Titan.
normal.cn: 天文学把它用于其他世界：土卫六的大气。

normal.en: The figurative sense grew in the late eighteenth century, when rooms and crowds got atmospheres.
normal.cn: 比喻义在十八世纪晚期发展起来，那时房间与人群开始有「气氛」。

abstract.en: Picture a thin blue shell wrapped around a stone in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一层薄薄的蓝色外壳裹住一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone lowers their voice at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间里所有人同时压低声音。

abstract.en: Picture a weight pressing on the shoulders of a whole crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一种重量压在整群人的肩上。

examples.en: The atmosphere thins quickly above the cloud layer.
examples.cn: 云层之上，大气迅速变稀薄。

examples.en: The hall had the atmosphere of a library after closing.
examples.cn: 大厅有一种闭馆后图书馆的气氛。

examples.en: The sample was sealed at one atmosphere of pressure.
examples.cn: 样品在一个大气压下被封存。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmos 是水汽，sphaira 是球：包住地球的一层汽球 → 大气层；人周围的「空气感」也就是气氛

root: 希腊 atmos「水汽」+ sphaira「球」→ 拉丁化 atmosphaera → 英语 atmosphere；atmos 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one envelope: the gas layer itself, the air inside it, the air of a room, the mood of a place, the tone of a work, the envelope of other worlds, a pressure unit, and finally any influence that seems to surround people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一层包层展开：气体层本身、层内的空气、房间里的空气感、场所的气氛、作品的基调、其他世界的气体包层、一个压强单位，最后是任何仿佛包围人的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin shell of gas wrapped around a solid body in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中一层薄薄的气体壳裹住一个固体。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SHELL: the envelope, the air within it, and the same shell around other worlds.
branches.cn: 物理外壳：包层、其中的空气，以及其他世界外围的同一层壳。

branches.en: ENCLOSED AIR: a room's air takes on a sensed character.
branches.cn: 封闭空气：房间的空气带上可感的性格。

branches.en: SHARED FEELING: a crowd and a work of art can both surround people with a tone.
branches.cn: 共享感受：人群与艺术品都能用一种调子包围人。

branches.en: THE MEASURING STICK: the envelope becomes a unit of pressure.
branches.cn: 量尺：这层包层变成一个压强单位。

branches.en: ABSTRACT PRESSURE: suspicion behaves like air and presses on everyone.
branches.cn: 抽象压力：猜疑行为像空气，压在每个身上。

intro.en: Atmosphere is a compound whose two Greek pieces also appear in other scientific words, and whose English descendants cover both weather and mood.
intro.cn: atmosphere 是一个复合词，两个希腊构件也出现在其他科学词中，其英语后裔同时涵盖天气与氛围。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin atmosphaera combines Greek atmos with Latin sphaera, and the English adjective atmospheric follows the Latin pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 atmosphaera 把希腊 atmos 与拉丁 sphaera 组合起来，英语形容词 atmospheric 沿袭这一拉丁模式。

items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指气体，而非球体。

items.example: The second piece gives the shape.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件给出形状。

items.meaning: the envelope of air around a body
items.example: The Latin coinage fixed the scientific term.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁造词固定了这个科学术语。

items.example: The atmosphere protects the surface.
items.exampleCN: 大气层保护地表。

items.example: Atmospheric pressure fell before the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴前气压下降。

items.example: The two sites differ atmospherically.
items.exampleCN: 两地在大气方面不同。

items.example: The receiver picked up atmospherics.
items.exampleCN: 接收机收到大气干扰。

items.meaning: a rare word for the airy envelope
items.example: Aerosphere appears in older texts.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本里出现这个词。

sceneCN: 这里 atmospheric 指「与大气压有关的」（第 3 个义项：大气压的）；句意为随着泵抽走空气，大气压把盖子压了下去。图中可辨识物件：玻璃箱、真空泵、下陷的盖子、压力表。

senses.title: Relating to the atmosphere
senses.definition: relating to the gas envelope of a planet
senses.definitionCN: 与行星的气体包层有关
senses.example: Atmospheric layers are named by how temperature changes with height.
senses.exampleCN: 大气各层按温度随高度变化的方式命名。
senses.why: the adjective attaches the noun atmosphere to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词 atmosphere 挂到它所描述的事物上。

senses.title: Produced in or by the atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 大气中发生的；大气造成的
senses.definition: occurring in the air or caused by processes within it
senses.definitionCN: 发生在空气中，或由其中的过程造成
senses.example: Atmospheric dust dimmed the sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 大气中的尘埃让落日变得黯淡。
senses.why: the envelope is also a workshop, and the adjective marks what goes on inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这层包层也是一间工坊，这个形容词标示在其中发生的事。

senses.title: Of atmospheric pressure
senses.definition: relating to the weight and pressure of the air
senses.definitionCN: 与空气的重量和压强有关
senses.example: Atmospheric pressure pushed the lid down as the pump withdrew air.
senses.exampleCN: 随着泵抽走空气，大气压把盖子压了下去。
senses.why: pressure is the atmosphere's most measurable behaviour, and the adjective marks that use.
senses.whyCN: 压强是大气最可测量的行为，这个形容词标示这一用法。

senses.title: Creating a mood
senses.definition: describing light, sound, design or writing that deliberately creates a mood
senses.definitionCN: 形容有意营造某种情绪的光线、声音、设计或文字
senses.example: The director used fog and low light for an atmospheric opening.
senses.exampleCN: 导演用雾与低照度营造了一个有气氛的开场。
senses.why: designers found that light and fog can wrap a space like air wraps a body.
senses.whyCN: 设计者发现光与雾能像空气包住天体那样包住空间。

senses.title: Having a strong mood
senses.definition: having a distinct and memorable feeling, as a place or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 如场所或音乐，具有鲜明而难忘的感觉
senses.example: The empty station was strangely atmospheric at night.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的车站在夜里有一种奇特的氛围。
senses.why: some places hold a feeling so strongly that the word for air becomes the word for it.
senses.whyCN: 有些地方强烈地留住一种感觉，以至于空气之词变成了感觉之词。

senses.title: Of atmospheric chemistry
senses.definition: relating to the chemical composition and reactions of the air
senses.definitionCN: 与空气的化学组成和反应有关
senses.example: Atmospheric chemistry tracks how ozone forms and breaks down.
senses.exampleCN: 大气化学追踪臭氧如何生成与分解。
senses.why: chemistry inside the air is a subject of its own, and the adjective labels it.
senses.whyCN: 空气内部的化学自成一门课题，这个形容词为它贴标签。

senses.title: Of emissions and pollution
senses.definition: relating to substances released into the air and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 与排入空气的物质及其影响有关
senses.example: Atmospheric carbon reached a new record last year.
senses.exampleCN: 大气中的碳含量去年创下新纪录。
senses.why: what enters the air becomes an atmospheric subject, and policy borrowed the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 进入空气之物成了大气课题，政策也借用这个形容词。

senses.title: Of other worlds' envelopes
senses.definition: relating to the gas envelopes of planets, moons or stars other than the earth
senses.definitionCN: 与地球以外行星、卫星或恒星的气体包层有关
senses.example: Atmospheric models of Titan predict methane rain.
senses.exampleCN: 土卫六的大气模式预测会有甲烷雨。
senses.why: other worlds have envelopes too, and models of them extend the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 其他世界也有包层，对它们的模拟延伸了这个形容词。

intro.en: Atmospheric is atmosphere plus the adjective suffix -ic, which goes back through Latin to Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: atmospheric 是 atmosphere 加形容词后缀 -ic，后者经拉丁语追溯到希腊语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Atmos 'vapour, steam' is of uncertain deeper origin; no reliable Indo-European source is established.
items.cn: atmos「水汽、蒸汽」的更深来源不确定，尚未确立可靠的印欧语来源。

items.en: Sphaira 'ball, globe' gave the second half of the noun atmosphere.
items.cn: sphaira「球、圆球」给出名词 atmosphere 的后半。

items.en: Atmosphaera was coined in seventeenth-century Latin science and passed into English in the 1630s.
items.cn: atmosphaera 在十七世纪拉丁科学中造出，并于十七世纪三十年代进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ic comes from Greek -ikos through Latin -icus; it turns the noun into a relational adjective.
items.cn: 后缀 -ic 经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos，把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.en: In the nineteenth century atmospheric extended from the physical air to anything that creates or carries a mood.
items.cn: 十九世纪，atmospheric 从物理的空气延伸到一切营造或承载气氛的事物。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first use of atmospheric is recorded, and it is usually placed in the late eighteenth or early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：atmospheric 的确切首见英语书证未被记录，通常放在十八世纪末或十九世纪初。

note.en: Group one holds closely related forms that are not this adjective; group two holds adjectives for air, weather and mood.
note.cn: 第一组是关系密切、却不是这个形容词的形式；第二组是表示空气、天气与氛围的形容词。

entries.definition: A rare fuller variant of the same adjective, found mainly in older prose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的罕见完整变体，主要见于较早的文字。

entries.definition: A plural noun for radio noise and mood effects; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无线电噪声与氛围效果的名词复数，并非这个形容词。

entries.definition: The noun itself; the adjective and the noun are often confused in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词本身；写作中这个形容词与名词常被混用。

entries.definition: A noun phrase built from the adjective; it names one quantity rather than a whole class of things.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个形容词构成的名词短语，指一个量而非一整类事物。

entries.definition: Full of air, light and space; it describes a room's feel, not the gas envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 空气充足、明亮开阔；描述房间的感觉，而非气体包层。

entries.definition: Relating to long-term climate; atmospheric concerns the air and its immediate conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 与长期气候有关；atmospheric 关心空气及其即时状况。

entries.definition: Relating to weather science and forecasting; atmospheric is the broader physical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 与气象科学与预报有关；atmospheric 是范围更宽的物理形容词。

entries.definition: Bringing a feeling or memory to mind; it overlaps with the mood sense but has no physical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 唤起感觉或记忆；与氛围义重叠，但没有物理含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: atmosphere plus -ic, the standard relational adjective suffix.
normal.cn: atmosphere 加 -ic，即标准的关系形容词后缀。

normal.en: The family runs atmosphere, atmospheric, atmospherically, atmospherics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 atmosphere、atmospheric、atmospherically、atmospherics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: atmospheric pressure, atmospheric science, atmospheric lighting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：大气压、大气科学、营造气氛的灯光。

normal.en: The mood sense is modern and common in reviews of films, hotels and music.
normal.cn: 氛围义较现代，常见于电影、酒店与音乐的评论。

normal.en: The rare variant atmospherical is longer but means the same.
normal.cn: 罕见变体 atmospherical 更长，但意思相同。

abstract.en: Picture a glass box whose lid sinks as the pump pulls air out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃箱，泵抽气时盖子向下陷。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor lit so dimly that every step feels important.
abstract.cn: 想象一条灯光极暗的走廊，每一步都显得重要。

abstract.en: Picture a thin blue line drawn along the edge of a planet.
abstract.cn: 想象沿行星边缘画的一条细蓝线。

examples.en: Atmospheric pressure falls as the weather front approaches.
examples.cn: 随着天气锋面逼近，气压下降。

examples.en: The production was praised for its atmospheric design.
examples.cn: 这部制作因营造气氛的设计受到称赞。

examples.en: Atmospheric models help predict conditions on other planets.
examples.cn: 大气模式有助于预测其他行星上的状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmosphere 是大气，-ic 是形容词后缀：大气的；后来人们把「有空气感」引申为「有氛围的」

root: 希腊 atmos「水汽」+ sphaira「球」→ 现代拉丁 atmosphaera → 英语 atmosphere；加 -ic（经拉丁 -icus 出自希腊 -ikos）→ atmospheric。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective outward: the envelope, what happens inside it, its pressure, the moods it can create, strong atmosphere, its chemistry, its emissions and the envelopes of other worlds.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词向外展开：气体包层、其中发生的事、它的压强、它能营造的情绪、浓烈的气氛、它的化学、它的排放，以及其他世界的气体包层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blue line drawn along the edge of a planet.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿行星边缘画的一条细蓝线。

branches.en: THE SHELL NEAR AND FAR: the same adjective covers our envelope and those of other bodies.
branches.cn: 近处与远处的外壳：同一个形容词既指我们这层，也指其他天体的那层。

branches.en: WHAT HAPPENS INSIDE: dust, chemistry and emissions are all processes within the air.
branches.cn: 其中发生的事：尘埃、化学与排放都是空气内部的过程。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: pressure is the envelope's most measurable behaviour.
branches.cn: 重量：压强是这层包层最可测量的行为。

branches.en: THE CRAFTED MOOD: light and sound can be arranged to wrap a space.
branches.cn: 刻意营造的氛围：光与声可以被安排来包住一个空间。

branches.en: THE MOOD THAT ARRIVES: some places hold a feeling without anyone arranging it.
branches.cn: 自然降临的氛围：有些地方无需安排就留住一种感觉。

intro.en: Atmospheric is a noun plus one suffix, and both halves are shared with a large scientific family.
intro.cn: atmospheric 是一个名词加一个后缀，两半都与一个庞大的科学词族共用。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin atmosphaera supplies the noun, and Latin -icus from Greek -ikos supplies the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 atmosphaera 提供名词，拉丁 -icus（出自希腊 -ikos）提供形容词词尾。

items.example: The first piece names the gas.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件指气体。

items.example: The second piece gives the shape.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件给出形状。

items.example: The atmosphere thinned with height.
items.exampleCN: 大气随高度变稀。

items.example: Atmospheric pressure pushed the lid down.
items.exampleCN: 大气压把盖子压了下去。

items.example: The valley is atmospherically sheltered.
items.exampleCN: 这个山谷在大气上受到屏障。

items.example: The storm filled the radio with atmospherics.
items.exampleCN: 风暴让收音机满是大气干扰。

items.example: Older books prefer atmospherical.
items.exampleCN: 较早的书更爱用这一完整形式。

items.meaning: a rare synonym for the envelope
items.meaningCN: 空气包层的罕见同义词
items.example: Aerosphere is mostly a historical term.
items.exampleCN: 这个词多半是历史术语。

latinEntries.meaning: the envelope of air around a body

definition_zh: 大气压；大气对单位面积表面施加的压强（海平面约为 1013 百帕）
definition_en: the pressure exerted by the weight of the atmosphere on a unit area of surface, about 1013 hectopascals at sea level
core_image: 一根细长玻璃管里的水银柱停在刻度旁，管外空气稳稳压住槽中的液面
scene: 实验室里，一根细长的玻璃管内水银面停在刻度旁，管外空气稳稳压住槽中液面。The mercury column rose as atmospheric pressure increased.
sceneCN: 这里 atmospheric pressure 指「大气对表面施加的压强」（第 1 个义项：大气压）；句意为随着大气压升高，水银柱上升。图中可辨识物件：玻璃管、水银柱、刻度尺、汞槽。

pos.zh: 大气压（不可数名词；指大气施加的压强）

forms.label: 复数（不同行星或不同地点的气压）

senses.title: The weight of the air
senses.definition: the pressure produced by the weight of the atmosphere on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 大气的重量压在表面上所产生的压强
senses.example: Atmospheric pressure falls by about one hectopascal for every eight metres climbed.
senses.exampleCN: 每上升约八米，大气压下降约一百帕。
senses.why: air has weight, and weight spread over an area is pressure; the phrase simply names that result.
senses.whyCN: 空气有重量，重量摊在一个面积上就是压强；这个说法只是在为那个结果命名。

senses.title: The weather reading
senses.definition: the value read from a barometer and used to describe weather systems
senses.definitionCN: 从气压计读出、用来描述天气系统的数值
senses.example: The forecaster watched atmospheric pressure fall all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员整个下午都在看大气压下降。
senses.why: meteorology needs one number for the state of the air, and pressure is that number.
senses.whyCN: 气象学需要用一个数字表示空气状态，压强就是这个数字。

senses.title: Standard sea-level pressure
senses.definition: the agreed average pressure at sea level, used as a reference and as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 公认的海平面平均气压，用作基准与单位
senses.example: Instruments are compared against standard atmospheric pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器都对照标准大气压进行比较。
senses.why: a reference value lets stations at different heights compare their readings.
senses.whyCN: 有了基准值，不同高度的台站才能比较读数。

senses.title: Pressure falling with height
senses.definition: the decrease of pressure with altitude, because less air lies above
senses.definitionCN: 气压随海拔升高而降低，因为上方空气更少
senses.example: Atmospheric pressure at the summit is barely two thirds of the sea-level value.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的大气压还不到海平面数值的三分之二。
senses.why: the higher you stand, the shorter the column of air above you, so the pressure must drop.
senses.whyCN: 站得越高，头顶的空气柱越短，压强必然下降。

senses.title: High and low systems
senses.definition: the pattern of relatively high or low pressure that shapes winds and weather
senses.definitionCN: 相对高压或低压所形成、并塑造风与天气的格局
senses.example: A low atmospheric pressure centre drew the storm northward.
senses.exampleCN: 一个低压中心把风暴吸向北方。
senses.why: wind blows from high to low pressure, so the map of pressure becomes a map of weather.
senses.whyCN: 风从高压吹向低压，因此气压图就成了一张天气图。

senses.title: Effect on boiling
senses.definition: the influence of pressure on the temperature at which a liquid boils
senses.definitionCN: 气压对液体沸腾温度的影响
senses.example: At high altitude the lower atmospheric pressure lets water boil sooner.
senses.exampleCN: 在高海拔，较低的大气压使水更早沸腾。
senses.why: boiling happens when vapour pressure matches the surrounding pressure, so the surrounding air sets the temperature.
senses.whyCN: 沸腾发生在蒸气压与外界压强相等时，因此外界空气决定了沸点。

senses.title: Altimeter setting
senses.definition: the reference pressure set into an altimeter so that it reads true altitude
senses.definitionCN: 为让高度表读出真实高度而设定的基准气压
senses.example: The pilot set the altimeter to the local atmospheric pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员把高度表设定到当地大气压。
senses.why: an altimeter measures pressure, not height, so it must be told the pressure at a known level.
senses.whyCN: 高度表测的是压强而非高度，因此必须告诉它某一已知高度的气压。

senses.title: Units of measurement
senses.definition: the units and scales in which the quantity is reported, such as hectopascals or millimetres of mercury
senses.definitionCN: 报告这一量值时所用的单位与标度，如百帕或毫米汞柱
senses.example: The station reports atmospheric pressure in hectopascals.
senses.exampleCN: 该台站以百帕报告大气压。
senses.why: a quantity needs a scale, and the old mercury column and the modern metric unit both remain in use.
senses.whyCN: 一个量需要标度，旧的水银柱与现代的公制单位至今都还在用。

intro.en: The phrase joins the Greek-based noun atmosphere with Latin-based pressure. Its scientific use grew from seventeenth-century experiments on air. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的名词 atmosphere 与拉丁来源的 pressure 组合起来，其科学用法来自十七世纪对空气的实验。年代均为约数。

items.en: Atmos 'vapour' and sphaira 'ball' were joined in modern Latin as atmosphaera for the envelope of air around a body; atmos is of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: atmos「水汽」与 sphaira「球」在现代拉丁中组合为 atmosphaera，指包住天体的空气层；atmos 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Latin pressura 'a pressing' comes from premere 'to press, squeeze', and gave English pressure through Old French.
items.cn: 拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」出自 premere「压、挤」，经古法语给出英语 pressure。

items.en: Torricelli's mercury tube showed in 1643 that the air holds up a column of mercury, which made atmospheric pressure a measurable quantity.
items.cn: 托里切利的水银管在 1643 年表明空气能托住一段水银柱，这使大气压成为可测量的量。

items.en: The fixed phrase atmospheric pressure spreads in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries as barometers become common instruments.
items.cn: 随着气压计成为常见仪器，atmospheric pressure 这一固定说法在十七、十八世纪传播开来。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries standards bodies fixed a standard sea-level pressure for comparing instruments and for aviation.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，标准机构确定了海平面标准气压，用于比较仪器并供航空使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first English use of the full phrase is not recorded and is usually placed in the seventeenth century, while the deeper origin of atmos is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一完整短语在英语中的确切首见未被记录，通常放在十七世纪；atmos 的更深来源同样没有定论。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on the same words that name something else; group two holds the genuine alternatives for the same quantity.
note.cn: 第一组是同样用这些词构成、却指别的事物的说法；第二组才是同一量值的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: The hyphenated form used before a noun, as in atmospheric-pressure sensor; it is the same quantity acting as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 放在名词前时加连字符的形式，如大气压传感器；仍是同一个量充当修饰语。

entries.tag: only one word of the phrase
entries.definition: The adjective alone describes the air, not the pressure; it is not a synonym for the quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 单独这个形容词描述空气，而非压强；它不是这一量值的同义词。

entries.definition: A defined reference pressure used as a unit; it is a fixed number, while atmospheric pressure varies.
entries.definitionCN: 作为单位使用的确定基准压强；它是一个固定数值，而大气压会变化。

entries.definition: A plainer phrase for the same thing, used in weather talk and in tyres; the formal term is atmospheric pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一事物的更朴素说法，用于谈天气与轮胎；正式术语是 atmospheric pressure。

entries.definition: The same quantity named after the barometer that measures it; common in weather reports.
entries.definitionCN: 同一量值以测量它的气压计命名，常见于天气报告。

entries.definition: Pressure adjusted to the height of sea level so that stations at different altitudes can be compared.
entries.definitionCN: 折算到海平面高度的气压，便于不同海拔的台站相互比较。

entries.definition: The pressure measured at the actual surface of a place, without reduction to sea level.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地实际地表测得的压强，不折算到海平面。

entries.definition: The everyday term; it also covers enclosed air, which atmospheric pressure does not.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法；它还涵盖密闭空间中的空气，而大气压不涵盖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Atmosphere supplies the air, pressure supplies the force per area.
normal.cn: atmosphere 提供空气，pressure 提供单位面积上的力。

normal.en: The phrase runs atmosphere, atmospheric, atmospheric pressure, barometric pressure.
normal.cn: 这一串是 atmosphere、atmospheric、atmospheric pressure、barometric pressure。

normal.en: Torricelli's mercury tube is the classic picture of the quantity.
normal.cn: 托里切利的水银管是这个量值的经典图像。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its uses: sea-level pressure, low pressure, altimeter setting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：海平面气压、低压、高度表设定。

normal.en: It falls with height and controls boiling, wind and weather.
normal.cn: 它随高度下降，并控制沸腾、风与天气。

abstract.en: Picture a column of mercury held up by nothing but air.
abstract.cn: 想象一段水银柱，全靠空气托住。

abstract.en: Picture a hill where every step removes a slice of the air above you.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山，每走一步就削去头顶的一片空气。

abstract.en: Picture a map painted in two colours, high and low, with wind running between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一张两色地图，高压与低压之间跑着风。

examples.en: Atmospheric pressure at the coast is higher than at the pass.
examples.cn: 海岸的大气压高于山口。

examples.en: A rapid fall in atmospheric pressure often precedes a storm.
examples.cn: 大气压迅速下降往往预示风暴。

examples.en: The altimeter must be set to the local atmospheric pressure.
examples.cn: 高度表必须设定到当地大气压。

dict_mnemonic.text: atmosphere 是大气，pressure 是压强：大气压住地面所施加的压强就是大气压；水银柱的高度就是它的读数

root: 希腊 atmos「水汽」+ sphaira「球」→ 现代拉丁 atmosphaera → atmosphere；拉丁 premere「压」→ pressura → pressure；组合为 atmospheric pressure。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measurable quantity: the weight of the air, its weather reading, its standard value, its fall with height, its high and low centres, its effect on boiling, its use in altimeters and its units.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个可测的量展开：空气的重量、天气读数、标准值、随高度下降、高低压中心、对沸点的影响、在高度表上的用途，以及它的单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mercury column held up by the weight of the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段被空气重量托住的水银柱。

branches.en: THE QUANTITY AND ITS SCALE: weight over area becomes a number with units.
branches.cn: 量值与其标度：面积上的重量变成一个带单位的数值。

branches.en: WEATHER: the reading and the pattern of highs and lows drive wind and storms.
branches.cn: 天气：读数与高低压格局驱动风与风暴。

branches.en: THE REFERENCE: a fixed sea-level value lets instruments and places be compared.
branches.cn: 基准：固定的海平面数值让仪器与地点可以比较。

branches.en: HEIGHT AND BOILING: less air above means lower pressure, which lowers the boiling point.
branches.cn: 高度与沸腾：上方空气更少意味着气压更低，沸点也随之降低。

branches.en: AVIATION: an altimeter is a pressure meter that must be told the local reference.
branches.cn: 航空：高度表是一台压强计，必须被告知当地基准。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two learned borrowings, one Greek in shape and one Latin, and both halves bring their own families.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个学术借词构成，一个带希腊形态，一个来自拉丁语，两半都带来各自的词族。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin atmosphaera supplies the first half, Latin pressura the second; Latin sphaera and premere stand behind them.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 atmosphaera 提供前半，拉丁 pressura 提供后半；其背后是拉丁 sphaera 与 premere。

items.example: The air is named as vapour in the first half.
items.exampleCN: 前半把空气称作水汽。

items.example: The envelope is pictured as a ball.
items.exampleCN: 这层包层被想象成一个球。

items.meaning: the gas envelope of a body
items.example: The atmosphere has weight.
items.exampleCN: 大气有重量。

items.example: The verb gives the idea of something bearing down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出「向下压」的意思。

items.example: The pressure rose with depth.
items.exampleCN: 压强随深度增加。

items.example: Atmospheric layers differ in temperature.
items.exampleCN: 大气各层温度不同。

items.example: Atmospheric pressure pushes the lid down.
items.exampleCN: 大气压把盖子压下去。

items.example: Barometric readings track the same quantity.
items.exampleCN: 气压计读数追踪同一个量值。

latinEntries.meaning: the envelope of air around a body

definition_zh: 压力；压强；血压；心理压力；催逼；紧迫的负担
definition_en: the force pressing on a surface per unit area; also the feeling of strain, or the act of urging someone to do something
core_image: 一只手掌按在桌面上，桌板把整份重量分散到整个接触面
scene: 潜水员下潜到十米深处，耳膜被水压压得发紧，呼吸也变得费力。The pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
sceneCN: 这里 pressure 指「单位面积上所受的力」（第 1 个义项：压力、压强）；句意为每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。图中可辨识物件：潜水员、面罩、深度绳、气泡。

pos.zh: 压力；压强（物理量）
心理压力；催逼；紧迫的负担

senses.title: Force per unit area
senses.definition: the force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface
senses.definitionCN: 作用在表面上的力除以该表面的面积
senses.example: Pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
senses.exampleCN: 每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。
senses.why: Latin pressura named a pressing, and physics gave the word a precise ratio of force to area.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 pressura 本指「压」，物理学给了这个词「力与面积之比」的精确含义。

senses.title: Pressure in a gas or liquid
senses.definition: the internal pressure of a fluid, measured in pascals or bar
senses.definitionCN: 流体的内部压强，以帕或巴计
senses.example: The gas pressure in the cylinder doubled when it was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 钢瓶受热时，瓶内气体压强翻倍。
senses.why: fluids push outward in all directions, and the word measures that push.
senses.whyCN: 流体会向各个方向推，这个词测的就是这种推力。

senses.title: Blood pressure
senses.definition: the force with which blood presses against the walls of the arteries
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁施加的力
senses.example: His blood pressure rose during the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 他在攀登过程中血压升高。
senses.why: medicine applied the physical word to the body's own plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个物理词用到人体自身的管道上。

senses.title: Psychological strain
senses.definition: the mental strain produced by demands that seem to exceed one's capacity
senses.definitionCN: 由似乎超出承受能力的要求造成的心理紧张
senses.example: The pressure of the final week kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周的压力让她睡不着。
senses.why: something weighing on the mind behaves like a weight on a surface, so the physical word serves feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 压在心头的东西行为像压在表面上的重量，于是物理词也服务感受。

senses.title: Social pressure
senses.definition: the influence of a group that pushes a person toward a particular choice
senses.definitionCN: 群体推动个人做出某种选择的影响
senses.example: Peer pressure made the younger students hide their doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴压力让年纪较小的学生藏起自己的疑虑。
senses.why: a group can press on a person as steadily as a hand on a table.
senses.whyCN: 群体能像按在桌上的手一样，稳稳地压住一个人。

senses.title: The act of urging
senses.definition: the act of repeatedly urging or persuading someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 反复催促或说服某人采取行动的行为
senses.example: The committee applied pressure until the report was released.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不断施压，直到报告被公布。
senses.why: pressing someone is the literal action of the Latin verb, carried into social life.
senses.whyCN: 催促某人正是那个拉丁动词的字面动作进入社会生活。

senses.title: The burden of demands
senses.titleCN: 工作与时间的紧迫负担
senses.definition: the weight of urgent work, deadlines or expectations
senses.definitionCN: 紧急工作、截止期限或期待带来的重负
senses.example: The staff worked under constant pressure during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 旺季期间员工一直在压力下工作。
senses.why: time and tasks can also pile up like a physical load.
senses.whyCN: 时间与任务也会像实物一样堆积起来。

senses.title: A weather system
senses.definition: a region of high or low atmospheric pressure shown on a weather map
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上标出的高压或低压区域
senses.example: A deep low pressure system crossed the coast overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一个深厚的低压系统一夜之间越过海岸。
senses.why: meteorology uses pressure as the variable that organises the whole map.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把气压当作组织整张天气图的变量。

intro.en: Pressure comes through Old French from Latin pressura 'a pressing', a noun from premere 'to press, squeeze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pressure 经古法语来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，它是 premere「压、挤」的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze, hold down'; its past participle pressus lies behind the noun and the English verb press.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤、按住」，其过去分词 pressus 是名词与英语动词 press 的来源。

items.en: Pressura 'a pressing, pressure' was formed from the participle and used for the act and its result.
items.cn: pressura「压、挤压」由分词构成，既指动作也指结果。

items.en: Old French pressure and Latin pressura gave English pressure in the late fourteenth century, first meaning anguish or the act of pressing.
items.cn: 古法语 pressure 与拉丁 pressura 在十四世纪末给出英语 pressure，最初指痛苦或按压的动作。

items.en: The force-per-area sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when experiments on air and fluids needed a precise term.
items.cn: 单位面积受力的物理义从十七世纪有记录，当时对空气与流体的实验需要一个精确术语。

items.en: Blood pressure appears in the eighteenth century, while the figurative senses of urgency and coercion grow from the same idea of something weighing down.
items.cn: 血压的用法出现在十八世纪，而紧迫与催逼的比喻义都从「有东西压下来」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: First English dates approximate: the earliest English use is usually dated to the late fourteenth century and the first physics citation to the seventeenth, though neither date is exact.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：英语最早用法通常定在十四世纪末，最早的物理书证定在十七世纪，但两者都不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same verb that are not the noun; group two holds nouns for force, strain and tension.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词来的形式、却不是这个名词；第二组是表示力、紧张与张力的名词。

entries.definition: The verb means to push down; as a noun it means the printing machines or the news media, not force per area.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为向下按；作名词指印刷机或新闻界，而非单位面积上的力。

entries.definition: To keep the air in a cabin or tank at a chosen pressure; it acts on a space, not on a person's mind.
entries.definitionCN: 让机舱或容器中的空气保持某一压强；作用于空间，不作用于人的心理。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means urgent; as a noun it means an act of ironing or a batch of records.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为紧迫的；作名词指熨烫动作或一批唱片。

entries.definition: Describing someone who is subjected to pressure; it is not the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容承受压力的人；并非名词本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for strain on a person or material; pressure is the force, stress is often the response.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或材料所受紧张的更宽泛词；pressure 偏力，stress 常指反应。

entries.definition: The deformation or damage caused by a load; it describes the effect rather than the pushing force.
entries.definitionCN: 载荷造成的变形或损伤；描述结果，而非推力。

entries.definition: A pulling force along a rope or a nervous stretch; the opposite direction from pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿绳的拉力或神经上的紧绷；方向与压力相反。

entries.definition: A push or pull without reference to area; pressure is force divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 不涉及面积的推或拉；pressure 是力除以面积。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin premere 'press' gives press, pressure, pressurize, pressing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 premere「压」给出 press、pressure、pressurize、pressing。

normal.en: Physics defines it as force divided by area; the unit is the pascal.
normal.cn: 物理学把它定义力除以面积，单位是帕。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: under pressure, blood pressure, high pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：在压力之下、血压、高压。

normal.en: The same word serves a diver's mask, a hospital ward and a committee room.
normal.cn: 同一个词服务潜水员的面罩、医院病房与委员会会议室。

normal.en: A weather map is drawn in pressure, with highs and lows.
normal.cn: 天气图以气压绘制，标出高压与低压。

abstract.en: Picture a palm flat on a table, the weight spread across the whole contact.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平放在桌上，重量摊在整个接触面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning toward one person until that person moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人向一个人倾压过去，直到那人让步。

abstract.en: Picture a column of water above a small mask, growing heavier metre by metre.
abstract.cn: 想象一小块面罩上方的水柱，一米一米地变重。

examples.en: The pressure inside the tank was too high for the valve.
examples.cn: 罐内压力对阀门来说过高。

examples.en: She felt the pressure of the deadline all week.
examples.cn: 她整个星期都感到截止期的压力。

examples.en: A low pressure system brought rain to the coast.
examples.cn: 一个低压系统给沿海带来降雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: press 是「压」，-ure 是名词后缀：压下去的那个力量 → 压力；物理上是单位面积上的力，心上就是心理压力

root: 拉丁 premere「压、挤」→ pressus → pressura「压」→ 古法语 pressure → 英语 pressure；引申为血压、心理压力与气压。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressing force: the physical quantity, the pressure inside a fluid, blood pressure, mental strain, group pressure, the act of urging, the burden of urgent work and finally a weather system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种压下的力展开：物理量、流体内压、血压、心理紧张、群体压力、催逼的动作、紧迫工作的重负，最后是一个天气系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat palm on a table, its weight spread over the whole contact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只平放的手掌，重量摊在整个接触面上。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL RATIO: force over area, and the same push inside a fluid.
branches.cn: 物理比值：力除以面积，以及流体内部的同一种推。

branches.en: THE BODY'S PLUMBING: blood presses on artery walls.
branches.cn: 人体的管道：血液压住动脉壁。

branches.en: THE INNER LOAD: strain and the pile of urgent demands both weigh on a person.
branches.cn: 内在负荷：紧张与堆积的紧急要求都压在人身上。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL PUSH: a group can press, and so can a committee.
branches.cn: 社会推力：群体能施压，委员会也能。

branches.en: THE WEATHER MAP: pressure becomes the variable that organises highs and lows.
branches.cn: 天气图：气压成为组织高低压的变量。

intro.en: Pressure is a Latin noun built on a verb, and that verb also gives the everyday English word press.
intro.cn: pressure 是建立在动词上的拉丁名词，那个动词也给出日常英语词 press。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and pressura 'a pressing' stand behind pressure, press, pressurize and pressing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 premere「压」与 pressura「压、挤压」是 pressure、press、pressurize 与 pressing 的来源。

items.example: The verb is the physical act behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是每个义项背后的物理动作。

items.example: The noun names the act and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指动作及其结果。

items.example: Pressure rose with depth.
items.exampleCN: 压强随深度上升。

items.meaning: to push down; the news media
items.example: Press the lid down firmly.
items.exampleCN: 把盖子稳稳压下。

items.meaning: to keep a space at a chosen pressure
items.example: The cabin is pressurized for flight.
items.exampleCN: 机舱为飞行增压。

items.meaning: kept at higher than ambient pressure
items.example: A pressurized tank stores the gas.
items.exampleCN: 加压罐储存这种气体。

items.meaning: the act of keeping a pressure
items.example: Pressurization keeps the cabin comfortable.
items.exampleCN: 增压让机舱保持舒适。

items.example: A pressing matter needed an answer.
items.exampleCN: 一件紧迫的事需要答复。

items.example: Barometric pressure tracks the weather.
items.exampleCN: 气压计读数追踪天气。

definition_zh: 空气压力；气压（可指大气压，也常指轮胎、气球等密闭空间内的气压）
definition_en: the pressure exerted by air, either by the atmosphere or by air enclosed in a space such as a tyre or a balloon
core_image: 一只轮胎被气泵充得鼓起，胎壁绷紧，手指按下去很硬
scene: 修车铺里，技师把气枪接到轮胎气门，表盘上的指针慢慢抬起。He checked the air pressure in all four tyres before the drive.
sceneCN: 这里 air pressure 指「密闭空间内空气的压强」（第 3 个义项：轮胎等密闭空间的气压）；句意为他在出发前检查了四条轮胎的气压。图中可辨识物件：气泵、气枪、轮胎气门、压力表。

pos.zh: 空气压力；气压（不可数名词）

forms.label: 复数（不同空间或行星的气压）

senses.title: Pressure exerted by air
senses.definition: the pressure that air exerts on the surfaces it touches
senses.definitionCN: 空气对它所接触的表面施加的压强
senses.example: Air pressure kept the suction cup against the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 空气压使吸盘贴在玻璃上。
senses.why: the phrase is the plainest name for the force air applies, whether enclosed or open.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法是空气所施力最朴素的名字，无论密闭还是敞开。

senses.title: The atmosphere's pressure
senses.definition: the pressure of the open atmosphere, the everyday name for atmospheric pressure
senses.definitionCN: 开阔大气的压强，即大气压的日常说法
senses.example: Air pressure fell sharply before the storm arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴来临前气压急剧下降。
senses.why: weather talk prefers the short phrase, while scientific writing uses the longer one.
senses.whyCN: 谈天气偏爱短说法，科学写作则用更长的正式说法。

senses.title: Pressure inside a tyre or ball
senses.definition: the pressure of air enclosed in a tyre, balloon or ball
senses.definitionCN: 封闭在轮胎、气球或球内的空气压强
senses.example: He checked the air pressure in all four tyres before the drive.
senses.exampleCN: 他在出发前检查了四条轮胎的气压。
senses.why: an enclosed space makes the phrase countable in practice: each tyre has its own pressure.
senses.whyCN: 密闭空间使这个说法在实际中可数：每条轮胎都有自己的气压。

senses.title: Working pressure in pneumatics
senses.definition: the pressure at which compressed air operates tools and machinery
senses.definitionCN: 压缩空气驱动工具与机械时的工作压强
senses.example: The workshop runs its tools at six bar of air pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个车间以六巴的气压驱动工具。
senses.why: industry needs a controlled supply, and the phrase names the working value.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要受控的气源，这个说法就指工作数值。

senses.title: Pressure in ducts and cabins
senses.definition: the pressure of moving or conditioned air inside ducts, cabins and buildings
senses.definitionCN: 风道、客舱与建筑内部流动或调节空气的压强
senses.example: Cabin air pressure is kept close to the value at a moderate altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 客舱气压保持在中等海拔的数值附近。
senses.why: ventilation and flight both manage air as a working medium, and pressure is the variable they control.
senses.whyCN: 通风与飞行都把空气当工作介质，压强就是它们控制的变量。

senses.title: Sound pressure
senses.definition: the tiny rapid variations in air pressure that carry sound
senses.definitionCN: 携带声音的空气压强的微小快速变化
senses.example: A loudspeaker produces sound by making rapid air pressure changes.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器靠制造快速的空气压强变化来发声。
senses.why: sound is a wave of pressure, so acoustics borrowed the everyday phrase for a precise quantity.
senses.whyCN: 声音是一种压强波，声学便借用这个日常说法来指一个精确量。

senses.title: Wind pressure on structures
senses.definition: the force that moving air exerts on a building, bridge or tower
senses.definitionCN: 流动空气对建筑、桥梁或塔施加的力
senses.example: Engineers tested the tower against extreme wind pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试这座塔能否承受极端风压。
senses.why: wind is moving air, and its push on a surface is measured as pressure.
senses.whyCN: 风是流动的空气，它对表面的推挤以压强来计量。

senses.title: Pressure changes and the body
senses.definition: the effects of changing air pressure on ears, lungs and blood at altitude or underwater
senses.definitionCN: 在高原或水下，气压变化对耳、肺与血液的影响
senses.example: The descent made the air pressure change faster than her ears could equalise.
senses.exampleCN: 下潜时气压变化太快，她的耳朵来不及平衡。
senses.why: the body is a pressure vessel too, so physiology uses the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 人体也是一个压力容器，因此生理学使用同一个说法。

intro.en: Air pressure joins the old Germanic word air, borrowed through Latin and Greek, with Latin-based pressure. The compound belongs to the scientific English of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
intro.cn: air pressure 把经拉丁语与希腊语借入的古日耳曼词 air 与拉丁来源的 pressure 组合起来，这一复合说法属于十七、十八世纪的科学英语。

items.en: Greek aēr meant 'lower air, mist', as opposed to aithēr, the bright upper layer. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊 aēr 指「低层空气、雾」，与指明亮上层的 aithēr 相对。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Latin aer and Old French air carried the word into English, where it replaced older native terms for the lower atmosphere.
items.cn: 拉丁 aer 与古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，取代了较早表示低层大气的本族词。

items.en: Pressure comes from Latin pressura 'a pressing', from premere 'to press'.
items.cn: pressure 来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，出自 premere「压」。

items.en: Once the barometer showed that air has weight, air pressure became a fixed phrase in experimental writing.
items.cn: 一旦气压计表明空气有重量，air pressure 就成了实验写作中的固定说法。

items.en: In later use the phrase spread to tyres, balloons and pneumatic tools, where the air is enclosed rather than atmospheric.
items.cn: 在后来的用法中，这个说法扩展到轮胎、气球与气动工具，那里的空气是封闭的而非大气的。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of aēr and first date): the pre-Greek source of aēr is not established, and the first English use of the compound is not exactly dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（aēr 的来源与首见年代）：aēr 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，这一复合说法在英语中的首见也没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds closely related phrases that name a different thing; group two holds the real alternatives for the same pressure.
note.cn: 第一组是关系密切、却指另一事物的说法；第二组才是同一种压强的真正替代说法。

entries.definition: The hyphenated form used before a noun, as in air-pressure gauge; it is the same quantity as a modifier.
entries.definitionCN: 放在名词前时加连字符的形式，如气压表；仍是同一个量充当修饰语。

entries.definition: A machine that raises air pressure; it produces the quantity rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 提高空气压强的机器；它产生这个量，而不是这个量本身。

entries.definition: A local region of different air, often felt in flight; it names a place, not a pressure value.
entries.definitionCN: 一块空气状况不同的局部区域，飞行中常有感觉；指位置，不指压强数值。

entries.definition: The movement of air; it describes motion, while air pressure describes push.
entries.definitionCN: 空气的流动；描述运动，而 air pressure 描述推力。

entries.definition: The formal name for the open atmosphere's pressure; air pressure is its everyday and broader counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 开阔大气压强的正式名称；air pressure 是其日常且范围更宽的对应说法。

entries.definition: The pressure inside a tyre; it is the commonest everyday use of air pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 轮胎内部的压强；是 air pressure 最常见的日常用法。

entries.definition: Pressure as read by a barometer; common in weather reports.
entries.definitionCN: 气压计读出的压强；常见于天气报告。

entries.definition: The controlled pressure inside an aircraft cabin; a specialised case of enclosed air pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机客舱内受控的压强；是密闭空气压强的一个专门情形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: air plus pressure: the push that air itself exerts.
normal.cn: air 加 pressure：空气本身施加的推挤。

normal.en: The family runs air, air pressure, atmospheric pressure, pressurize.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 air、air pressure、atmospheric pressure、pressurize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the enclosures: tyre pressure, cabin pressure, air-pressure gauge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出密闭场合：轮胎气压、客舱气压、气压表。

normal.en: Weather talk uses the short phrase; scientific writing prefers atmospheric pressure.
normal.cn: 谈天气用短说法，科学写作更爱用 atmospheric pressure。

normal.en: Sound is a rapid series of air pressure changes.
normal.cn: 声音是一连串快速的空气压强变化。

abstract.en: Picture a tyre swelling until the wall feels hard under a thumb.
abstract.cn: 想象轮胎鼓起，直到拇指按上去胎壁发硬。

abstract.en: Picture a suction cup staying on glass because the air outside keeps pushing.
abstract.cn: 想象吸盘贴在玻璃上，因为外面的空气一直在推。

abstract.en: Picture a sound wave as a ripple of squeezed air moving toward an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象声波是一圈被挤压的空气向耳朵推进。

examples.en: Check the air pressure before a long drive.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶前先检查气压。

examples.en: Air pressure in the cabin is kept near a moderate altitude value.
examples.cn: 客舱气压保持在接近中等海拔的数值。

examples.en: A sudden change in air pressure can make ears ache.
examples.cn: 气压骤变会让人耳朵疼。
